results.title: Ball detector v2: weak labels for the ball in flight (pass corridors, flight-time negatives, ranking loss, calibrated p), tuned on a held-out match
results.summary: On T, I measured where 51 visually confirmed in-flight balls sit (97 when V's are included). The median offset from the line between passer and receiver is 1.2 m (90th percentile 3.5 m). In pixels the median is 6 px (90th percentile 28 px). The ball runs ahead of the constant-speed point by +0.10 of the pass length (median). Only 49% of these balls fall inside v1's 2.5 m "between" bag, and 96% are at least 1 m from every player. v2 replaces the gap bags with corridor bags along every completed ground pass: within 2.5 m on the ground or 20 px of the passer-receiver line, inside a time window centred on a decelerating-ball model. The same frames supply negatives: every player body outside the corridor, landmarks, and everything beyond 6 m / 48 px. That attacks v1's main in-flight failure: 12 of its 19 wrong top-1 picks on T were within 2 m of a player. Ball-free patches go from 724 to about 6,000, with landmark and goal-line hard negatives. The loss adds a size-invariant bag pool, an in-patch softmax ranking term with a "no visible ball" option, and a term that pushes down the strongest wrong peaks; afterwards a 2-parameter Platt fit calibrates p. Tuning moves to a held-out match U (M5) with an automatic corridor measure: checked against the blind judgements on T it has precision 0.97 and recall 0.91, where the registered 1 m rule had recall 0.34. A placebo (false-hit) check guards against a model that learns the empty grass between team-mates. V is then used once (its 2nd of 3 variants), extended with four new M2/M10 windows for statistical power.

changes.what: New patch kinds, cut in one stream per half. (1) 'flight': each completed ground PASS (>=10 m, >=0.8 s, team-mate receiver), and each intercepted PASS whose next event is an opponent PASS/DRIVE/HIGH PASS within 0.8-4 s, at s in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} + U(-0.08, 0.08) of the pass time. The centre is the predicted ball point t_hat(s) = s + 0.4 s(1-s) along A->B, jittered ±48 px. (2) 'lofted': HIGH PASS/CROSS at s in {0.35, 0.65}. (3) 'free': 2 ball-free patches at every second action frame with track status 1/2. Centres are at least 12 m from both the actor and the track point, split by category: player clusters 35%, landmarks 25%, a strip 2 m inside the touchlines/goal lines 25% → 15%, random pitch 25%. Keep 'action' as v1. Patch size 320 px for every kind (the corridor window's median extent is 168 px; 88% fit within 300 px). Store A, B, s, t_hat, pass length and the event ids per patch. Halves: both halves of M3, M4, M6 and M8. For the 2nd halves of M4, M6 and M8, skip frames 13,500-21,000 (T plus a 1.5 min buffer). M5, M1, M2, M10, M7 and M9 are never cut for training.

Add corridor(), curtain() and landmark_cells(). Codes for flight patches: bag (1) = cells whose ground point is within 2.5 m perpendicular of A->B, OR within 20 px of the projected centreline, for t in [max(t_hat-0.22, 2 m/L, 0.08), min(t_hat+0.28, 1-1.5 m/L, 0.95)], plus 1.0 m x sx px above (bounce). Cells inside any player body box, or within 1.0 m of a player's feet, become 0. Ignore (0): within 6 m or 48 px of the whole segment, plus a 2 m-height curtain above it. Hard negative (-3): the body box of every player whose feet are at least 1.0 m outside the bag, passer and receiver included, and this OVERRIDES ignore; also landmarks outside the ignore band. Everything else is -1. Keep a bag only if at least 85% of its cells are in the patch; otherwise retry with t_hat-0.15..+0.20, else drop. Lofted patches get no bag. Their curtain is the segment up to clip(0.3 L, 3, 15) m x sx px plus a 4 m / 32 px ground band, set to 0. Players inside the curtain are 0, players outside are -3, the rest -1. Free patches: -1 everywhere. Bodies are -3, and landmarks are -3 in a 0.75 m (min 12 px) disk; the landmarks are the penalty spots, centre spot, corners, halfway/touchline crossings, goal posts, box corners and 6-yard corners. Run COCO sports-ball (conf >= 0.25) on each free patch; detections not within 1 m of a landmark become a 1 m ignore disk (spare/resting balls are not called 'not a ball'). Drop the v1 'between after PASS' bags; keep the dribble bags (1.5 m around the dribbler) as kind 'dribble'.

Pools and mix per batch of 16 (320 px): flight 5, action 3, dribble 1, lofted 1, free 6 (landmark 2, cluster 2, strip 1, random 1). Bag pool is size-invariant LSE: z_bag = (1/4)·log Σexp(4z) − (1/4)·log 4, then BCE(z_bag, 1). Add an in-patch ranking term λ=0.5: −log(Σ_bag e^z / (Σ_{bag∪neg} e^z + e^{z_null})), where z_null is a learned scalar (init 0) for a hidden ball. Negatives: focal γ=2 with ×3 on -3 cells (as v1), plus plain BCE on the top-16 negative 5x5 local maxima per patch (weight 1 per patch). Normalise by patch count, not bag count. Drop-worst from step 1,500: flight 25%, action 15%, dribble 25%. Stem frozen for 1,000 steps. 5,000 steps with cosine decay; checkpoints 3000/4000/5000. Add scale jitter ×[0.8, 1.25] and motion blur p=0.15 (0-7 px). Variant B (optional): at step 3,000, take the model's peak inside each flight bag. Replace the bag by a 0.75 m disk around that peak when p >= 0.8, the margin over the second bag peak is >= 0.3, and the peaks for the 3 frames of that pass are monotone in t at 5-35 m/s. Then continue to 5,000.
detect() takes an optional calibration (a, b) and returns p_cal = σ(a·logit + b). Add load_calibration() reading <checkpoint>.calib.json. No architecture change.

Platt fit on U only. Inputs: the logits of the top-8 peaks per measured frame (eval --save with raw logits). Labels: correct when the automatic corridor rule holds (flight frames), or when within 1.5 m of the actor or track point (PASS/DRIVE frames). Writes a, b, the reliability table and tau. tau = the smallest p_cal giving <= 1.0 candidates per frame on U random frames AND top-1 precision >= 0.8 on U flight+action frames.

Add (1) 'corridor flight hit': a top-1 ground point within 2.5 m of A->B or within 20 px of its projection, and >= 1.0 m from every player, over the 4 middle-half frames per pass. (2) 'placebo': the same rule at 2 frames 0.6-1.2 s before the kick of passes whose passer has held the ball for >= 0.8 s, restricted to t in [0.2, 0.9]. Any hit there is a 'line prior'. (3) Store raw logits of the top-8 peaks. Keep every registered v1 measure unchanged.

Add corridor decoys: random points inside the corridor, >= 1 m from players. Add one-frame-per-pass selection across several detectors (v2, v1, COCO) in one shuffled set, and record which tiles repeat earlier judgements (judge test-retest).

Use p_cal and tau from the calibration json. Optionally flag a 'resting' candidate: within 3 px for >= 10 s with no player within 3 m, its p multiplied by 0.2. The flag's on/off is chosen on U events only.

Written before any v2 patch is cut. Contains the label constants above, the U/V/V-ext windows, the selection rules, gate G2, the V claims and the events-retune grid. It also records v1's and COCO's automatic corridor-hit on V from the existing V.json, computed when the protocol is frozen and before v2 exists.
New subsection 'Ball detector v2: the ball in flight' after results. It lists every deviation (V extended, M5 held out, T demoted to descriptive, auto measure replacing the 1 m rule).

Cut U windows st2_118577_2nd_f015000, st2_118577_1st_f060000 and st2_118577_2nd_f045000; st2_118577_1st_f030000 already exists. Cut V-ext windows st2_117093_1st_f037500, st2_117093_2nd_f015000, st2_132877_1st_f037500 and st2_132877_2nd_f015000. Streams the GSR of M3 2nd, M5 2nd, M2 2nd and M10 2nd once (cached parquet).

results.data_and_labels:
TRAINING MATCHES: M3, M4, M6, M8, both halves (8 halves). The 2nd halves of M4/M6/M8 drop frames 13,500-21,000, so T plus a buffer stays out. M5 (118577) is held out entirely as the unseen-match tuning set U. M1 is excluded (other camera); M2/M10 are V; M7/M9 are test, never touched.

VOLUMES (counted from cached BAS+GSR):
- Completed ground passes >= 10 m, >= 0.8 s: 202-355 per half (median about 300). Median length 15.5-17.7 m, median duration 1.5-1.7 s.
- Intercepted passes: about 15-25 per half.
- HIGH PASS 39-77 and CROSS 7-31 per half. Ground PASS >= 35 m: 0-2 per half.
- Expected patches:
  - flight: about 2,400 passes × 3 frames × 0.9 fit ≈ 6,400 corridor bags;
  - lofted: about 600 passes × 2 ≈ 1,200 negative patches;
  - action: about 7,000 bags (v1 kept 85% of action patches);
  - dribble: about 1,200;
  - free: about 6,000 ball-free patches (v1: 724).
- About 21k JPEGs at 320 px, about 1.3 GB in .cache, never committed.

CORRIDOR GEOMETRY, from my check of v1's blind keys on T: 51 confirmed in-flight balls (97 with V's, quoted only as a cross-check).
- Distance perpendicular to the A->B segment:
  - median 1.19 m, 75th percentile 2.14, 90th 3.52, 95th 6.0;
  - share <= 1 m: 0.42; <= 2 m: 0.73; <= 3 m: 0.87.
- In pixels to the projected segment: median 6 px, 75th percentile 14, 90th 28, 95th 34.
  - Far side: larger in metres (median 1.9 m) but not in pixels (6 px).
  - Near side: 0.73 m, 11 px.
  - So the bag is the union of a metric rule and a pixel rule.
- The ground point sits about 0.9 m further from the camera than the segment (median); 61% of balls are above the segment in the image. Hence the 1 m × sx extension upwards.
- Along the pass: t − s has median +0.10 and 5-95% range [−0.13, +0.41], so the ball runs ahead of constant speed (deceleration). Centre on t_hat = s + 0.4 s(1−s) with window [−0.22, +0.28].
- Only 49% of these balls lie within v1's 2.5 m between-bag around the constant-speed point. Most v1 flight supervision was wrong or missing.
- Coverage of the chosen corridor (2.5 m | 20 px, time window, 0.8-1.2 m player exclusion): 0.82-0.86 of confirmed balls.
  - This is selection-biased upward (only balls a detector found).
  - Drop-worst at 25% absorbs the rest, including occluded and chipped balls.
- Every confirmed ball lay within 6 m or 48 px of the segment, so cells beyond that are safe negatives.
- 96% were >= 1 m and 86% >= 2 m from every player. Mid-flight, all player bodies more than 1 m outside the bag are safe hard negatives; this is the v1 feet failure (12 of 19 wrong top-1 picks on T within 2 m of a player).
- Which frames: s in [0.17, 0.83] only, at least 2 m from the passer and 1.5 m from the receiver along the line; 3 frames per pass (adjacent frames add nothing).
- Lofted (HIGH PASS/CROSS): no positives, only negatives outside a height curtain.

FREE PATCHES:
- Only at action frames where actor and track agree within 3 m, so the ball's position is known. Every patch cell is >= 12 m away.
- Landmarks are hard negatives. COCO's penalty spots were 14 of its 19 wrong confident picks on V.
- Off-landmark COCO balls are ignored, not called negatives: a resting ball by a goal is a real ball, and calling it 'not a ball' would teach that ball-like objects are not balls.

Patch-level label noise budget: event-frame timing ±0.2 s ≈ ±0.12 in s, the 1.05 × 0.68 m position grid, and calibration 0.3-0.8 m are all inside the widths above.
results.training:
Model unchanged: ResNet-18 at stride 8 with a stride-4 lateral and a 1-channel head, so the label and loss changes are what v2 tests.

Steps: 5,000 at batch 16 of 320 px patches. Mix: 5 flight, 3 action, 1 dribble, 1 lofted, 6 free. Learning rates: AdamW 3e-4 head / 1e-4 layer2 / 3e-5 early, 100-step warm-up, cosine decay. Stem and layer1 frozen for 1,000 steps. Seed 0.

Loss per patch, divided by 16:
1. Bag: BCE(z_bag, 1), with z_bag = LSE_r4 − log(4)/4. The pool is size-invariant: corridor bags have about 1,000 cells against v1's ~200, and v1's −log(N)/r term would force broad activation.
2. Ranking (λ 0.5): softmax over the patch's bag and negative cells plus a learned null logit. It targets top-1 directly, which is what every measure scores.
3. Focal negatives: γ 2, hard cells ×3.
4. Peak suppression: BCE on the 16 strongest negative local maxima. v1 filled its 8-candidate cap at tau <= 0.15.

Drop-worst from step 1,500: flight 25%, action 15%, dribble 25%. Augmentations: v1's set plus scale ×0.8-1.25 and light motion blur.

Variant A: as above. Variant B (optional): A, plus pseudo-label shrinking of flight bags at step 3,000, gated by confidence, margin and monotone peaks across the pass's 3 frames. Only one variant ever goes to V.

Time: 320² vs 256² is ×1.56, so about 1.1 s/step and about 90 min for A; B adds about 10 min of pseudo-labelling and 2,000 steps (about 40 min). 4 threads; nothing else heavy runs at the same time.

Monitor every 250 steps on 300 held-out training patches: bag hit (peak in bag), mean count of bag cells with p > 0.5 (peakiness; abort if > 30), and negative peaks with p > 0.15 per patch.
results.inference_and_tracking:
Single-frame detect() as v1: pitch crop, 5x5 local maxima, outline filter, sub-pixel refinement. The difference is p_cal = σ(a·logit + b), Platt-fitted on U. tau is chosen on U: the smallest p_cal giving at most 1 candidate per frame on random frames and top-1 precision of at least 0.8 by the automatic labels. Targets: at most 2 candidates per frame at p >= 0.15, against v1's 8.

Top-1 is used for every detector measure; at most 4 candidates per frame go to the events pipeline, as v1. The ground point is (u, v + size/2) through image_to_pitch. An in-flight ball reads about 0.9 m further from the camera; this is documented, not corrected.

In detect_ball_heatmap.py, an optional 'resting ball' down-weighting: a candidate static within 3 px for >= 10 s with no player within 3 m gets ×0.2. It is decided only by U events, because the match ball also rests at set pieces.

Linking stays in ball_tracking, with ball_time_aware and stride 2 as in v1. Cost as v1: about 1 s per full frame with 2 threads.
results.evaluation:
SPLITS:
- U (tuning; unseen match for v2; M5 1st half was in v1's training, so U favours v1, which is conservative): st2_118577_1st_f030000 plus 3 new M5 windows. About 75 passes, about 400 action frames, 200 random frames, about 150 placebo frames.
- T: descriptive only (same matches as training).
- V: M2/M10 minutes 10-13 of the 1st halves. 38 passes; the blind primary measure.
- V-ext (new, registered before v2 exists): 4 more M2/M10 windows, about 75 more passes, for the automatic measure. That gives about 113 passes.
- Test M7/M9: untouched.

AUTOMATIC MEASURE, validated before use. Corridor flight hit (2.5 m | 20 px, >= 1 m from every player), checked against the blind T judgements on 122 free-flight tiles: precision 0.97 (77/79), recall 0.91. The registered 1 m rule had recall 0.34. Over the 48 T passes × 4 frames it gives v1 0.71 vs COCO 0.51 (+0.21 [0.13, 0.28]), matching blind T's 0.75 vs 0.58.

SELECTION ON U (frozen in protocol v3): among A@{3000, 4000, 5000} and B@{4000, 5000}, the best U corridor flight hit. Within 0.02 of the best, prefer A, then the later step. Subject to:
- placebo <= 0.05;
- action hit >= v1's on U − 0.05.

GATE G2 ON U (all must hold, else stop and report U):
1. Corridor hit, v2 − COCO >= 0.10 with bootstrap lower bound > 0, and v2 − v1 lower bound > 0.
2. Placebo <= 0.05.
3. Blind U check (about 110 tiles): one frame per pass for v2 and COCO, 10 random decoys, 10 corridor decoys. Requires:
   - v2 match-ball-in-play rate >= 0.65;
   - decoys judged B <= 2/20;
   - precision of the automatic measure against the judge, on v2's picks, >= 0.9. If this fails, the automatic measure is demoted on V and blind is the only primary.

V CLAIMS (variant 2 of 3):
- Primary E3v2: blind free-flight on V's 38 passes (the 2nd of the 4 frames). Tiles are v2 + v1 + COCO top-1 (114) plus 6 random and 6 corridor decoys, 126 tiles, shuffled, judged before the key is read. Claim 'better than COCO in free flight on unseen matches' if the exact McNemar test on discordant passes gives p < 0.05 with more v2-only hits. v2 vs v1 is reported the same way. Agreement with the old tiles_ffV judgements on repeated v1/COCO tiles is reported as judge test-retest.
- Co-primary, only if G2(3) held: corridor hit over V+V-ext, about 113 passes × 4 frames, paired bootstrap over passes. Requires a 95% lower bound > 0 vs COCO; vs v1 is reported. Holm across the 2 primaries vs COCO.
- Secondary:
  - registered 1 m geometric hit;
  - placebo;
  - action hit vs a random point;
  - candidates per frame at tau on random frames;
  - blind precision of 40 confident v2 picks (p_cal >= tau) plus 20 decoys, 60 tiles (COCO's 40 from E4 reused; disclosed);
  - ECE of p_cal on those picks.

POWER: with 38 passes, McNemar needs roughly a 10-2 discordant split (as on T), so it detects only about +0.2. With 113 passes the bootstrap SE is about 0.027, so the automatic measure detects about +0.08.
results.expected_effect:
The main gain is fewer wrong top-1 picks on players in flight. v1 had 12 of its 19 wrong picks on T within 2 m of a player; v2 now sees about 6,400 flight frames where every player body is a hard negative. Free-flight bags go from wrong half the time (49% coverage) to about 85% coverage.

Expected on V:
- Blind free-flight: v2 0.65-0.75 (25-28/38), against COCO 0.58 and v1 0.50. A formal McNemar win over COCO on 38 passes is about a coin flip.
- Automatic corridor hit on V+V-ext: v2 ≈ 0.70-0.80 against COCO ≈ 0.50 (T levels), so a lower bound > 0 is likely if the true gain is >= +0.1.
- Candidates per frame at p >= 0.15: from 8 down to <= 2.
- Precision of confident picks: >= 0.8 kept.
- Action hit: about the same (0.40-0.50), since the feet supervision is kept at 3-4 of 16 per batch.
- Placebo: <= 0.05.

Events after the U retune: pass+carry F1 about 0.47-0.52 against 0.44, and shots cut from 182 to fewer than 60. The F1 interval may still include 0 with 130 labels.
risks: Line prior: corridor bags could teach 'empty grass between team-mates', and the corridor measure would reward exactly that. Guards: the placebo measure, corridor decoys in blind tiles, the G2 blind check, and the in-patch ranking term with null.

The geometry was measured only on balls that v1 or COCO found (n=51 on T). True corridor coverage, including occluded and chipped balls, is probably about 0.75-0.8, not 0.85; drop-worst 25% is the hedge.

Holding out M5 leaves 4 training matches instead of v1's 5, though with both halves. Generalisation to unseen matches could suffer; refitting on 5 matches is deliberately not done, so that what is gated is what goes to V.
The automatic measure was validated on v1/COCO picks. It may not transfer to v2; G2(3) re-checks it blind on U and demotes it if precision < 0.9.
Large bags with a size-invariant pool can be satisfied by broad activation. Monitor peakiness and negative peaks; the peak-suppression term counters it.
Ignoring off-landmark COCO balls may raise picks of resting balls (B*); the optional resting filter is decided on U events only.
Ball height: in-flight ground points are biased about 0.9 m away from the camera, which affects shot and goal geometry in events.
Small samples: U has about 75 passes and V 38, so blind power is limited. V-ext changes V's definition and must be registered before v2 runs and disclosed.
Compute and network: 4 GSR streams (2.7 GB each) plus 8 half-video streams. If HF range requests throttle, the build can double to about 2 h.
Event retune on about 170 U labels can overfit; mitigated by the coarse grid and the simplest-within-0.02 rule. Events on V run once.
evidence_checked: SOCCERTRACK_V2.md sections on the ball detector and on events, and the code of build_ball_patches.py, build_ball_labels.py, train_ball_heatmap.py, src/ball_heatmap.py, eval_ball_detector.py and ball_tiles.py.

v1 bags were mostly at feet: 4,622 action, 1,944 between, 724 negative (labels.parquet: action 4,622, between 1,944, negative 724 over 5 first halves). The between bags were positive-only, at half weight, 2.5 m around the constant-speed point.

Scripts: scratchpad/ball/dev_analysis.py and dev2-dev9.py. Using v1's judged keys plus score files (ground point (u, v+size/2) through image_to_pitch), on T (n=51) the confirmed in-flight ball's perpendicular distance to passer->receiver has median 1.19 m, 75th percentile 2.14, 90th 3.52, 95th 6.0. Pixel distance: median 6.2 px, 75th 14, 90th 28.
Far side median 1.9 m / 6 px; near side 0.73 m / 11 px (pooled T+V). The ground point is biased about 0.9 m away from the camera; 61% of balls are above the segment in the image.
t − s on T has median +0.10 and 5-95% range [−0.13, +0.41]: the ball runs ahead of constant speed. Only 49% lie within v1's 2.5 m between-bag around the interpolated point.
Confirmed in-flight balls are >= 1 m from every player 96% of the time and >= 2 m 86%. All lie within 6 m or 48 px of the segment.

Automatic rule (2.5 m | 20 px, >= 1 m from players) against blind judgements on 122 T free-flight tiles: precision 0.97, recall 0.91 (the 1 m rule: recall 0.34). On T: v1 0.714, COCO 0.505 (+0.21 [0.13, 0.28]).
Wrong top-1 picks on T. v1: 19, of which 8 within 1 m of a player, 4 at 1-2 m, 3 off the pitch and 1 resting ball. COCO: 34, of which 20 resting balls and 11 on lines.

Completed ground passes >= 10 m, >= 0.8 s: 202-355 per half. Median length 15.5-17.7 m, duration 1.5-1.7 s. HIGH PASS 39-77 and CROSS 7-31 per half; intercepted passes 15-25 per half; ground PASS >= 35 m: 0-2.
The corridor time window, projected, spans a median of 168 px, with 88% <= 300 px, so 320 px patches are needed.

Local resources: GSR is cached for M3 1st, M4/M6/M8 both halves, M5 1st, M2 1st and M10 1st (the 1st half of M1 is also cached; it stays excluded); M3 2nd, M5 2nd, M2 2nd and M10 2nd must be streamed. 24 GB disk free, 15 GB RAM, 4 cores idle.

results.title: Ball detector v2: a motion-aware heatmap with pass-corridor labels and a linker in pitch metres, tuned on a held-out match (M6) and judged blind on an enlarged V
results.summary: v2 keeps the v1 heatmap network (ResNet-18 to stride 8 with a stride-4 lateral) and adds motion to its input. The network now sees frame t, its signed differences to t-2 and t+2, and its difference to a 28-second running-median background: 12 channels. The ImageNet RGB stem is kept as it is, and a zero-initialised 9-channel motion conv is summed into it, so training starts exactly where v1 started. A synthetic benchmark puts the cost at about +7% for inference and +18% per training step. The labels add what v1 lacked: pass-corridor bags along every completed ground pass with negatives outside them, point labels from a classical blob miner (used only if a blind check finds them at least 90% correct), and about 12,000 streamed ball-free patches aimed at penalty spots, goal mouths and touchline balls. Training uses both halves of M3, M4, M5 and M8; M6 is held out entirely as an unseen tuning match, and M6 is also where COCO picked resting balls, like M2's penalty spots. Candidates are linked in pitch metres by a Viterbi linker: it allows direction changes only near detected players and penalises static tracks. On V, v1's top-1 was in the pass corridor on 49% of free-flight frames, but some candidate in its top 3 was on 66%, so re-ranking alone has room. Every choice is made on M6; V gets one new pre-registered window per validation match (about 76 passes) so a "clearly better" claim can be tested by exact McNemar on blind tiles. Events are then retuned on M6 only and scored once on V. Estimated cost: about 16 hours of machine time and four blind checks of about 100-120 tiles each.

changes.what: Shared by extraction, mining and inference. (1) background(samples): per-pixel median of 15 frames at t + 2 s*j, j=-7..7, clipped at half or window edges (at least 8 samples), uint8; (2) motion_channels(prev, cur, nxt, bg): D- = cur-prev, D+ = cur-nxt, F = cur-bg as signed float /255, each divided by a fixed per-channel std measured once on 1,000 training strips and stored as constants; (3) mine(prev, cur, nxt, bg, bag_mask, cal, person_boxes): classical constant-velocity blob miner. Blobs are max-channel |I-B| > max(20, 3*MAD), outside dilated person boxes, area 0.25-4x the ball's pi(d/2)^2 with d = 0.22 m * max(sx, sy), aspect ratio <= 3. A triple (c-, c0, c+) with c0 inside the bag passes when the step mismatch is <= max(2 px, 0.25*|c+ - c-|/2), the ground speed is 2-35 m/s and its direction cosine to the pass is >= 0.5 when faster than 4 m/s. A point label is returned only when exactly one triple passes.

Store one 1024x256 JPEG strip (q95) per sample: [t-2 | t | t+2 | background crop] at the same location. While decoding, every 50th frame goes into a 15-deep deque (about 200 MB). Patches wait in a queue until the sample 14 s after t arrives; their background crop is then the median over the region (about 15 ms each). New kinds: 'corridor' (completed ground passes: PASS, team-mate receiver, >= 8 m, >= 0.6 s, frames at 30/50/70% of the pass, centred on the linearly interpolated point with +-48 px jitter) and 'negative' (streamed from every half: 4 per sampled in-play frame, ball status != 0, >= 20 m from the ball track and >= 150 px from it in u). The negatives are 40% on players, 20% on landmarks (penalty spots, centre spot, goal mouths, corners), 20% on 60 px strips along the touchlines and goal lines (spare balls, ball boys) and 20% random on the pitch, about 1,500 per half. 'action' and 'between' are kept (between: DRIVE-opened gaps, and PASS gaps not used as corridors). No sample is cut during HIGH PASS, CROSS or SHOT flights. --half 1/2; the M6 matches 118578, 117092 and the test matches are refused.

Corridor labels: the positive bag is every cell within 3.0 m of the passer(frame a) -> receiver(frame b) GSR segment with fraction s in [s_lin(t)-0.2, s_lin(t)+0.3] (a decelerating ball runs ahead of linear), extended 2 m upwards in the image for chips. An ignore band runs to 4.5 m and 4 m high; beyond it cells are negative; other players' bodies are hard negatives (-3); passer and receiver are ignored. A bag is dropped if less than 75% of it is inside the strip (most near-side long passes are lost; those balls are 12-16 px and easy anyway). Mined labels: when motion_bg.mine finds exactly one ball, the bag becomes a 0.4 m disk around it (rest of the corridor ignored) and the row is flagged mined=True. Action bags as in v1, but FREE KICK is dropped: a ball still for more than 14 s is in the background. Negative strips: all cells -1, bodies -3. Ball-size estimates use max(sx, sy). Codes format unchanged (64x64 int8).

build(motion=True): conv1_rgb (ImageNet 3->64, 7x7/2) plus conv1_motion (9->64, 7x7/2, weights initialised to 0, no bias), summed before bn1; the rest is unchanged (about 2.9 MB of weights). to_tensor_v2(prev, cur, nxt, bg) gives a 12-channel tensor. detect_v2(model, prev, cur, nxt, bg, outline, tau=0.05, top_k=8, cal): same crop, padding and peak logic as detect(), with size = 0.22*max(sx, sy). v1's build() and detect() stay for comparison.

Strip loader. The same flip and photometric jitter go to all 4 crops; JPEG re-encoding is drawn per crop. Temporal reversal (swap t-2 and t+2) with p=0.5. Motion dropout with p=0.1 (prev=next=cur, bg=cur) so the net degrades gracefully. MIX = action 4, corridor 4 (mined bags when available), between 1, negative 7. conv1_motion trains from step 1 at lr 3e-4; RGB stem and layer1 frozen to step 800 as in v1. 6,000 steps, cosine schedule, worst-bag drop from step 1500 (action 15%, corridor 25%, between 25%). Checkpoints at 3000, 4500 and 6000. --no-motion runs the ablation (same loader, motion channels forced to 0). --exclude-matches defaults to 117092 118578.

v2 path. Pass 1 grabs every 50th frame and keeps pitch-bbox crops for the background (about 90 x 6.4 MB per 3-min window). Pass 2 decodes in order with a 5-frame ring buffer and runs detect_v2 at every even frame plus any --extra-frames (the odd measured frames of the evaluation). The background is recomputed whenever its centre moves 50 frames (about 2.5 s each, about 4 min per window). Writes all candidates with p >= 0.05, at most 8 per frame, as tracks rows (detection_method 'heatmap_v2').

Ball linker in pitch metres for the calibrated path. Each candidate's ground point is image_to_pitch(u, v + size/2). Measurement covariance J^-1 diag(1.5 px)^2 J^-T, from the local 2x2 Jacobian, so a far-side depth error of about 0.75 m is not a jump. Stage A, tracklets: a constant-velocity Kalman filter (sigma_a 8 m/s^2, 40 m/s^2 within 1.5 m of a detected player), Hungarian association at chi2 9.21, spawned at p >= 0.2, ended after 3 missed frames. This gives each candidate a velocity and a 'static for >= 2 s' flag. Stage B: first-order Viterbi over (candidates + a null state) per detection frame. Unary is logit(p) - logit(tau). Transition is the Mahalanobis distance of b from a's prediction; Q is inflated near players (kicks, receptions); there is a soft speed cap at 35 m/s, a static penalty for tracklets static >= 2 s and >= 3 m from every player, and a null cost per frame. Player positions come from the pipeline's own detections (never ground truth). Output: at most one row per frame. Fixed physics parameters; only the null cost and the static penalty are tuned on T2 (4x3 grid). Takes about 1 s per window.

In the to_pitch (calibrated) branch, use ball_link.link(...) instead of ball_selection.select_single_ball when the flag --ball-linker is set. The current call uses one px_per_m from player heights, while this panorama spans 2-72 px/m, so its speed gate is off by up to about 10x. Broadcast path unchanged.

--candidates PARQUET (raw or linked rows) as an alternative to running detectors inline; v2 inline needs t+-2 frames and the background, so it is easier from the dense parquet. Adds the automatic 'corridor hit': top-1 ground point within 3 m of the passer-receiver segment, t in [0.05, 0.95], >= 1 m from every GT player, over all four frames per pass. Checked against 162 blind-judged v1/COCO tiles: agreement 0.90, kappa 0.78, 1 false hit. The registered 1 m measure is kept for continuity. The linked pick falls back to the raw top-1 when the linker says 'no ball', so linking only re-ranks. Output in the same JSON format for ball_tiles.py.

--reuse DIR (carry over old judgements for v1/COCO picks at the same frame, never shown again); --rejudge N (mix N old judged tiles back in blind, to measure judge drift); --from-strips (tiles from training strips' centre frame, for the mined-label check); dedupe picks of different detectors within 6 px on the same frame into one tile, credited to each.

events.detect_events accepts a params dict that overrides the module constants (defaults unchanged). tune_events_st2.py caches each tuning window's metric tracks once (pipeline with the v2-linked ball, teams, to_pitch) and sweeps detect_events in-process (seconds per config). The objective is pooled (F1 - chance F1) for pass and carry at 1 s. Writes a frozen events_v2.json.

New section with protocol v3 (written before T2 is measured and before anything v2 runs on V), the deviations (M6 replaces old T; V extended by V+; automatic corridor measure introduced), results and caveats. Derived data (strips, windows, weights, candidates, tiles) stays in .cache/ and the scratchpad, never committed.

results.data_and_labels:
SPLIT. Train: both halves of M3 118575, M4 118576, M5 118577 and M8 128058, 8 halves. GSR is cached for six of them; the second halves of M3 and M5 must be streamed (about 5 min each). Tuning, T2: M6 118578, held out of v2 training entirely; v1 had trained on its first half. M6 is the tuning match because COCO picked resting balls there (11 of 17 pass tiles were 'B*'), like M2's penalty spots. M8 is easy (COCO 17/21, v1 19/21 on its second-half window) and would not discriminate. T2 windows: st2_118578_1st_f030000 (2 min, 7 passes), st2_118578_2nd_f015000 (17 passes), plus two new cuts with fetch_soccertrack_v2.py, 1st-half minutes 10-13 and 2nd-half minutes 25-28: about 60 passes and about 200 PASS/DRIVE. V: the old M2 and M10 1st-half minutes 10-13, plus V+ (new, registered before any v2 run) M2 and M10 1st-half minutes 30-33 (GSR cached): about 76 passes. M1 stays excluded (another camera); M7 and M9 are never touched.

STRIPS. Each sample is one 1024x256 JPEG q95, [t-2 | t | t+2 | background], about 164 KB (v1 patches were about 41 KB each). The offset k=2 is fixed a priori, not tuned: (a) inference runs at stride 2, so t+-2 are the neighbouring detection frames and cost no extra decoding; (b) at the median pass speed (10.5 m/s) the ball moves 0.84 m in 2 frames: 16 px laterally on the far touchline (ball 4.3 px), 60 px on the near one (ball 16 px), but only 1.7 px when moving in depth on the far side, where the background channel has to carry the signal; (c) consecutive frames are never identical (mean |diff| 1.0-2.8 on M3), so the motion signal is genuine. Background = median of 15 frames 2 s apart, centred on t (28 s span; one 4K median of 15 frames took 5.3 s, a 256 px crop takes about 15 ms). Per half, about 850 action, about 700 corridor (of about 300 passes x 3 frames, after near-side drops), about 300 between and about 1,500 negative strips: about 27,000 strips and about 4.5 GB in total (24 GB free).

LABELS (codes per 4x4 cell as in v1: 1 bag, 0 ignore, -1 negative, -3 hard negative).
(1) Action bags as in v1 (1.5 m around actor feet and track point; FREE KICK dropped).
(2) Corridor bags, new: the 3 m corridor around the passer-receiver segment, over s in [s_lin-0.2, s_lin+0.3], with negatives beyond a 4.5 m ignore band. The blind tiles show the ball 1.3-3 m off the line, and the judged balls lie a median 1.33 m (75th percentile 2.23 m) from it. Unlike v1's positive-only 'between' bags, these teach what is NOT the ball in flight, which is where v1 failed.
(3) Mined point labels, new: when the constant-velocity blob miner finds exactly one ball-sized triple in the corridor, the bag shrinks to 0.4 m. Gate S1, before training: 80 mined points + 20 decoys from training strips, blind; mined labels are used only if at least 90% are the match ball; otherwise corridor bags alone.
(4) Between bags: DRIVE gaps centred on the dribbler (1.5 m), positive only.
(5) About 12,000 ball-free strips instead of 724, aimed at the static distractors seen on V (penalty spots on M2, resting balls by goals on M6). In those strips the background channel makes 'static' learnable.
Labels come only from BAS and GSR of training halves. GSR person boxes (bx, by, bw, bh) are used only for mining and hard negatives in training, never at inference.
results.training: Model: v1's BallNet with a two-branch stem. conv1_rgb is ImageNet on frame t; conv1_motion takes the 9 channels D-, D+ and F (normalised signed differences), is zero-initialised and summed into the same 64 maps before bn1. At step 0 the net is exactly v1's ImageNet initialisation; the zero weights get non-zero gradients at once, because their inputs are non-zero. Stacking raw frames TrackNet-style with copied ImageNet weights would scramble the pretrained filters; the difference form is a linear re-parametrisation of the same 12 inputs with a clean start. Loss as in v1: log-mean-exp MIL (r=5) per bag, focal negatives (gamma 2), hard x3; corridor bags weight 1, between 0.5; worst 15% action and 25% corridor/between bags dropped from step 1500. Batch 16: action 4, corridor 4 (mined when available), between 1, negative 7. Augmentation: identical flip and photometric jitter across the 4 crops, per-crop JPEG re-encoding, temporal reversal p=0.5, motion dropout p=0.1. Schedule: 6,000 steps (about 3.5 epochs), AdamW, cosine with 100-step warm-up. Learning rates: head/lat 3e-4, conv1_motion 3e-4 from step 1, layer2 1e-4, RGB stem and layer1 3e-5 after unfreezing at step 800. Seed 0; checkpoints at 3000, 4500 and 6000. Cost: v1 measured 0.70 s/step on 4 threads; the synthetic benchmark gives x1.18 for the motion stem, plus about 0.1 s for loading 4 crops, so about 0.95 s/step and about 1.6 h. Ablation run: the same data, labels and steps with --no-motion (about 0.8 s/step, about 1.35 h). It separates the label effect from the motion effect, is measured on T2 only and never spends a V variant. Optional, only if S1 passes and T2 shows mined labels help: one round of self-training (v2 picks in corridors as new point labels). Not in the base plan.
results.inference_and_tracking:
DETECTION (detect_ball_heatmap.py, v2 path). Pass 1 grabs every 50th frame (cv2 grab: 751 frames decoded in 6 s) and keeps pitch-bbox crops. Pass 2 decodes in order with a ring buffer and runs detect_v2 at every even frame and at each odd measured frame. Input: the pitch bbox plus pads, about 3,900 x 650 px. Output: up to 8 candidates at p >= 0.05 with size 0.22*max(sx, sy). The background is recomputed every 50 frames (about 2.5 s on the bbox, about 4 min per 3-min window). Cost: the synthetic benchmark gives 2.01 vs 1.87 s/frame for motion vs v1 under load (+7%). With the measured v1 anchor (about 1 s/frame with 2 threads), v2 is about 1.15 s/frame alone, or about 80 min per 3-min window at stride 2 when two windows run in parallel (v1: 75). Gating the network to foreground tiles was considered and rejected: 31% of 256 px tiles hold foreground, but a 64 px halo makes the gated area about 0.7 of the frame, a gain of only about 1.4x, not worth the complexity.

LINKING (src/ball_link.py). The pipeline's select_single_ball uses one px_per_m for a panorama that spans about 2 px/m (far side, in depth) to 72 px/m (near side, along x), so its speed gate is wrong by up to about 10x. The v2 linker works in pitch metres, with Jacobian-based measurement noise. Stage A builds tracklets with a constant-velocity Kalman filter that allows large accelerations only within 1.5 m of a detected player, where kicks and receptions happen. Stage B is a Viterbi over candidates plus a null state, with tracklet velocity, a static penalty (tracklets static for >= 2 s and >= 3 m from every player: penalty spots, balls resting by goals) and a soft 35 m/s cap. Players come from the pipeline's own detections, never GT. On saved v1 candidates on V, the ball was among the top-3 on 66% of free-flight frames against 49% at top-1 (T: 71% vs 64%); COCO had almost no such headroom (53% vs 47% on V). So the linker matters for a candidate-rich detector. For the evaluation the linked pick falls back to the raw top-1 at frames without a ball (linking only re-ranks). For events the linked track, gaps included, becomes the ball rows. Compute: under 1 s per window.
results.evaluation:
REGISTERED FIRST (ball_protocol_v3.json, written before T2 is measured): splits as above; V+ windows chosen by rule (minutes 30-33), not by content; v2 = V detector variant 2 of 3; the RGB-only ablation and any 'v1 + linker' run stay on T2 only.

AUTOMATIC MEASURE. corridor-3m: top-1 ground point within 3 m of the passer-receiver segment, t in [0.05, 0.95], >= 1 m from every GT player, all four frames per pass. On 162 judged v1/COCO tiles it agrees with the blind judgements 0.90 of the time (kappa 0.78, 1 false hit, 16 misses); the registered 1 m measure reached kappa 0.30. Because v2 is trained on corridor bags it could game this measure, so it is only for tuning and secondary reporting. Its false-hit rate is re-checked on v2's own blind tiles.

T2 CHOICES (in order, all on M6):
(1) Checkpoint 3000/4500/6000 by raw corridor-3m top-1; the later one is kept when within 0.02.
(2) tau for 'confident' reporting: the smallest giving <= 1 candidate per frame on 50 random frames per window (the linker always gets p >= 0.05).
(3) Linker null cost x static penalty (4x3 grid) by corridor-3m on linked picks plus action hit. The linker is kept only if it beats raw by >= 0.03.
(4) Motion vs ablation: the motion model goes to V unless the ablation leads by >= 0.05 on corridor-3m (disclosed if so).
GATES:
S2, automatic: v2 corridor-3m must beat v1 by >= 0.10 and COCO by >= 0.15 on T2. v1 trained on M6's first half, so this is conservative for v2. Otherwise stop and diagnose.
G2, blind (one check, about 120 tiles): v2 top-1 at one frame per T2 pass (about 60), COCO on the windows without old judgements (about 43; the old M6 2nd-half judgements are reused), 15 decoys. Pass requires v2 blind hit >= 0.65, exact McNemar vs COCO p < 0.05, and corridor-3m false hits on v2's tiles <= 10%. If G2 fails, at most two further T2 iterations and no V.

V (REPORT, run once).
Primary: blind free-flight hit, one frame per completed ground pass (the second of the four, as in protocol v2), v2's linked pick vs COCO top-1 and vs v1 top-1. The claim needs exact McNemar on discordant passes, p < 0.05 after Holm over the 2 comparisons.
Check A (old V, about 118 tiles): 38 v2 tiles (v1/COCO judgements from tiles_ffV reused), 20 old tiles re-judged blind for drift (if agreement < 0.9, all old V tiles are re-judged together with v2's), and 40 v2 confident picks plus 20 decoys for precision (E4-style).
Check B (V+, about 115 tiles): v2, v1 and COCO top-1 at one frame per pass, deduped within 6 px, plus 15 decoys. v1 and COCO run on V+'s measured frames only (about 20 min).
Secondary: corridor-3m (all 4 frames), the registered 1 m measure, action hit at PASS/DRIVE, ball within 3 m of the actor, candidates per frame, Wilson intervals per detector, the paired bootstrap.

SAMPLE SIZE. With about 76 passes and v2 = 0.78 against COCO = 0.58, about 24 vs 9 discordant passes are expected (p about 0.01); at 0.75 it is borderline (p about 0.04). With old V alone (38 passes) a claim would need about 0.85, which is why V+ is added. The blind checks total about 470 tiles in 4 checks: S1 100, G2 120, A 118, B 115.
results.events_plan:
Order and isolation:
(1) Freeze v2 completely (checkpoint, tau, linker parameters) after G2 and before any events work. The detector never changes afterwards.
(2) Tuning windows TE = the four M6 windows (T2). The v2 ball there is out-of-sample, like on V; M6 is never in V; about 250 actions (about 100 PASS, about 90 DRIVE). Pipeline runs: st2_118578_1st_f030000 already has one; the other three need one (about 1 h each); V+ needs two.
(3) Per TE window, build once the metric tracks: pipeline players and teams, the v2-linked ball, to_pitch. tune_events_st2.py then sweeps detect_events in-process at seconds per config, instead of re-running the pipeline.
(4) Six parameters only, the ones that over-fire with a ball that is often present: POSSESSION_RADIUS_M {1.5, 2.5, 4, 8 (current)}, MIN_POSSESSION_HOLD_S {0.2, 0.4, 0.6}, POSSESSION_MAX_BALL_SPEED_KMH {30, 45, 60}, CARRY_MIN_TIME_S {0.8, 1.2, 1.6}, MIN_PASS_DISTANCE_M {0.3, 3, 6}, and a shot gate SHOT_MIN_KMH {10, 40, 60} x SHOT_MAX_DIST_FROM_GOAL_M {50, 30}. Search: coordinate descent, two rounds (about 40 configs).
(5) Objective: pooled (pass F1 - chance F1) + (carry F1 - chance F1) at 1 s over TE, which rewards matching rather than firing more; constraint: shots <= 3 x (SHOT + GOAL labels) + 2 per window. Among configs within 0.01 of the best, take the one with the fewest events (plateau, not peak); report leave-one-window-out stability.
(6) Register events_protocol_v3 (config, measures, claim rule) before V.
Primary on V: pass+carry F1 at 1 s pooled over old V + V+, v2 ball + retuned rules vs COCO ball + current rules, 10 s block bootstrap; an events gain is claimed only if the lower 95% bound > 0.
Decomposition, reported but not primary: v2 + current rules, COCO + retuned rules (separates the ball effect from the rule effect); per-group F1 vs chance per window; shot count vs labels; team and actor accuracy; ball within 3 m of the actor.
(7) Run once on V. Nothing is tuned on M2 or M10; there are no post-hoc rule edits after V. Any later change is a new protocol, scored on fresh minutes of M2/M10 or deferred to the test matches by explicit decision.
results.expected_effect:
Free flight on unseen matches:
- Blind hit on V + V+: about 0.70-0.80 for v2 (old V: v1 0.50, COCO 0.58). It comes from two sources. First, recall: motion and background channels make a moving 4-7 px blob salient, and the corridor negatives teach what is not the ball in flight; about 30% of V free-flight frames had no v1 candidate in the corridor at all. Second, ranking: the linker recovers part of the 0.17 top-1 vs top-3 gap.
- Corridor-3m top-1 on V: about 0.70 (v1 0.49, COCO 0.47).
- Precision of confident picks: >= 0.85 (v1 0.80, COCO 0.53).
- Penalty-spot and resting-ball picks near zero (static penalty plus background channel).
- Ball within 3 m of the actor at actions: about 0.60-0.70 (v1 0.52-0.55).
The far side remains the weak spot for balls moving in depth (about 1.7 px per 2 frames) and for chips and crosses (not labelled in flight). Chance that the registered V claim (p < 0.05 vs both COCO and v1) passes: roughly even. The ablation tells whether motion or labels did the work.

Events after retuning on M6:
- Event count about 1-1.5x labels (v1 heatmap: 3x).
- Shots cut from 182 to about the label scale.
- Pooled pass+carry F1 about 0.45-0.55 (COCO 0.35, v1 heatmap 0.44).
- With about 260 labels on V + V+ the bootstrap interval is about +-0.08, so an events gain is likely but not assured.
risks: M2 is the hard match (old V: v1 6/19, COCO 8/19 on M2 against 13/19 and 14/19 on M10) and is half of V + V+. If its failure is lighting or texture rather than static distractors, motion helps less there.

Far-side balls moving in depth barely move in the image (sy about 2 px/m on the far touchline gives about 1.7 px per 2 frames at 10.5 m/s). The background channel must carry those frames. High passes and crosses are not labelled in flight, and their ground projection misleads the linker.

The 28 s median absorbs anything still for more than about 14 s: dead balls before set pieces, a standing goalkeeper. FREE KICK action bags are dropped for that reason, and a restart ball may be missed (it is not in free flight, so the primary measure is unaffected).

Corridor bags and the corridor-3m measure share geometry, so v2 could learn a 'between team-mates' prior and look better on the automatic measure than it is. Mitigation: blind tiles stay primary, and the automatic measure's false-hit rate is re-checked on v2's own judged tiles (gate <= 10%).
Mined point labels are biased to easy, isolated balls, and a wrong unique triple would be a confident wrong label. They are used only if S1 finds at least 90% correct; otherwise corridor bags alone.

Holding out M6 leaves 4 training matches (8 halves). One seed, same rigs and league. The T2 gate on M6 may still flatter v2 if M6's static-ball distractor is unusually large; v1 on M6 is in-sample (trained on its first half), which makes the v1 comparison conservative for v2.
One judge who knows the hypothesis (blind only to the source); drift since the old V judgements. Mitigation: 20 re-judged tiles, and a full blind re-judge if agreement is below 0.9.
Extending V by V+ and replacing old T with M6 are protocol changes. They must be registered before any v2 run and disclosed; V's variant budget becomes 2 of 3 used.

Compute is about 16 h and dominated by dense stride-2 inference (8 windows, about 4.8 h) and five new pipeline runs (about 4 h). Other jobs share the CPU (one was running during this design), so wall time may be about 1.5x. If time is short, drop the ablation (-1.7 h) before V+.
Event tuning rests on one match (about 250 actions) and may not transfer. The small grid, the F1-minus-chance objective and the plateau choice limit it; the bootstrap interval may still include zero.
JPEG re-encoding of strips (q95) adds noise to 3-5 px balls and their differences; per-crop JPEG augmentation matches it at training, and inference reads the original H.264 frames.

The linker relies on the pipeline's player detections for kick zones. Missed or merged players make kicks look like velocity jumps, and the null state then drops real ball frames for events (the evaluation falls back to the raw top-1).
evidence_checked: Machine: 4 cores, 15 GB RAM, 24 GB free on /; another process (dev7.py) was using one core during this design.

Calibration scales (local_scale; M2, M3 and M8 agree within 0.5 px/m): far touchline centre sx 19.7 / sy 2.0 px/m (ball about 4.3 px); centre spot 31 / 4.9; near touchline 72 / 27 (ball about 16 px); far corners about 15 / 8; near corners about 14 / 30. detect() sizes the ball with sx only, which underestimates it at the near corners.

Completed ground passes (>= 10 m, >= 0.8 s, team-mate receiver) per half from cached BAS + GSR: M3-1 334, M4-1 305, M4-2 252, M5-1 202, M6-1 310, M6-2 249, M8-1 334, M8-2 270. Median length 15.3-17.7 m, duration 1.48-1.70 s, about 10.5 m/s. With >= 8 m / 0.6 s: 249-397 per half. 66-95 HIGH PASS / CROSS per half.
Measured passes per window (frames_of): M8 1st 7, M8 2nd 21, M6 1st 7, M6 2nd 17, M4 2nd 10, M2 19, M10 19. st2_118578_1st and st2_128058_1st are 2-minute windows (3,000 frames).
Old blind judgements by window. M8 2nd: v1 19/21, COCO 17/21 (easy). M6 2nd: v1 10/17, COCO 6/17 plus 11 resting balls. M2: v1 6/19, COCO 8/17. M10: v1 13/19, COCO 14/19.

Automatic corridor measure vs 162 judged v1/COCO free-flight tiles (tiles_ff + tiles_ffV): at 3 m, >= 1 m from players, t in [0.05, 0.95]: agreement 0.90, kappa 0.78, 1 false hit, 16 misses. The registered 1 m measure: agreement 0.60, kappa 0.30. Judged balls lie a median 1.33 m (75th percentile 2.23 m) from the passer-receiver line.
Re-ranking headroom from saved candidates (pass frames): v1 on V top-1 0.49, any of top-3 0.66, any of 8 0.70; v1 on T 0.64, 0.71, 0.76; COCO on V 0.47, 0.51, 0.53 (median 1 candidate per frame).

Video probe on a training window (M3): no duplicated frames (consecutive mean |diff| 1.0-2.8); decoding 751 4K frames with cv2 grab took 6.2 s; a 15-frame 4K median took 5.3 s; pixels above 25 against the background are 1.6% of the pitch, with 31% of 256 px tiles and 25% of 128 px tiles holding any; pitch bbox about 3830 x 560 px.

Synthetic benchmark (random weights, no video): a 9-channel zero-init motion stem adds +7% to a full-pitch forward (2.01 vs 1.87 s with 2 threads under load) and +18% to a batch-16 training step. Ratios are used against the measured anchors (0.70 s/step, about 1 s/frame).
v1 data: 9,088 patch JPEGs in 370 MB (about 41 KB each); labels: 4,622 action, 1,944 between, 724 negative. v1 training log: 3,000 steps in 2,147 s.

The pipeline's calibrated branch (score_soccernet.py) calls ball_selection.select_single_ball with one px_per_m from player heights before to_pitch; ball_selection's own notes say that 54-64% of frames offered exactly one candidate on the broadcast windows.

src/events.py constants for limited views: POSSESSION_RADIUS_M 8.0, SHOT_MIN_KMH 10, SHOT_MAX_DIST_FROM_GOAL_M 50, CARRY_MIN_TIME_S 0.8, MIN_PASS_DISTANCE_M 0.3. These are consistent with the v1 heatmap's 3x event count and 182 shots.
Pipeline outputs exist for M2, M3, M4-1st, M6-1st, M8-1st and M10 windows. One 2-minute pipeline run took about 41 min (clip.json 09:48 to tracks 10:30).
GSR cache holds 118575_1st, 118576_1st/2nd, 118577_1st, 118578_1st/2nd, 128058_1st/2nd, 117093_1st and 132877_1st. Second halves of M3 and M5 must be streamed; V+ uses first halves (cached).
Probe and benchmark scripts are in the scratchpad (v2design/fg_probe.py, bench.py, agree.py, headroom.py); nothing in the repo was changed.

results.title: Ball v2, then events: hold out M5 for tuning, grow V with fresh M2/M10 minutes, use a free-flight measure checked against the blind judgements, and tune event rules on out-of-fold balls
results.summary: Matches are the unit of generalisation. v2 (F) trains on both halves of M3, M4, M6 and M8, minus ±1 min around the old T windows, which stay as a seen-match diagnostic. All tuning happens on M5, a match F never sees: 6 windows, about 78 passes, gated by G1' before anything runs on V. V grows from 38 to about 200 passes with 8 fresh 3-min windows of M2 and M10 chosen now; the old V stays identical and reuses its v1 and COCO candidates and judgements. The primary measure is a new automatic free-flight measure (FF-auto): a 4 m corridor along the pass with a timing guard, at least 1 m from every player. It was chosen on the T judgements and agrees with the judge at kappa 0.82 on T and 0.81 on the old V; the registered 1 m rule scored 0.24 and 0.33. About 425 new blind tiles (100 on U, 325 on V) check that FF-auto is valid for v2 in particular and that the blind result points the same way; if the validity rule fails, a blind McNemar test becomes primary. Event rules are tuned on the 4 cached first-half windows with out-of-fold balls from two fold detectors (no tuning window's match is in its detector's training data), checked on M5 with F's balls, frozen, then measured once on 4 V windows. Error control: two families (detector, events) at alpha 0.025 each, a fixed order of tests within each; about 23 h CPU in total.

results.training:
**F (the v2 detector):**
- Recipe variants come from the label design. At most 3 are planned (hard cap 4), compared on U only.
- One seed (0), ResNet-18 stride 8 with stride-4 lateral as in v1 unless the recipe changes it.
- About 5,000 steps of batch 16, about 60 min with 4 threads, since there is 1.6x the data. Checkpoints at 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000.

**Choice rule, written before training:**
- Variant and checkpoint: highest U FF-auto, top-1 at any p. Within 0.02 of the best, the later checkpoint. Then higher U confident-pick precision.
- tau is label-free: the smallest grid tau giving at most 1.0 candidate per frame on U's random frames (50 per window, 300 in all). It is used only for events and for confident-pick tiles. FF-auto and the blind tiles use top-1 at any p.
- Optional: a second seed of the chosen recipe on U only (about 60 min), to report seed spread. Never run on V.
- F is not retrained with M5 added: what is tuned is what is reported.

**Folds A and B:**
- Frozen recipe, same steps and checkpoint index as F's choice, trained only after G1' is decided.
- Each fold's tau is calibrated label-free the same way, on the random frames of its own held-out E-tune windows.

**Provenance.** Each checkpoint stores its training matches, halves, excluded ranges, recipe hash and seed. The eval and detect scripts refuse windows from those matches.
results.inference_and_tracking:
**Ball evaluation:**
- Frame sets as v1 (frames_of, seed 0): 4 middle-half frames per completed ground pass (PASS of at least 10 m and 0.8 s, team-mate receiver), PASS/DRIVE frames, and 50 random frames per window.
- On V-old, v1 and COCO candidates are reused from V.json. Before v2 is scored, a regression run must reproduce V.json's registered 0.23/0.23 exactly.
- On V-new, v2, v1 and COCO all run on the same frames. Candidates are saved for tiles.
- FF-auto summaries are written sealed and opened only after the blind sittings are judged.

**Events:**
- detect_ball_heatmap.py at stride 2, 2 threads, two windows in parallel.
- Per-detector tau_cal; top-k chosen on E-tune from {1, 2, 4}.
- Balls are swapped into cached tracks and teams, so players and teams are identical across configurations. After that the path is unchanged: outline filter, ball_selection.select_single_ball, merge_fragments, to_pitch, ball_time_aware=True.
- No temporal ball tracker in v2: that would be a third V variant.

**Sequence and budget** (CPU wall-clock on 4 cores):
- **P0, prep, 1.5 h:**
  - GSR for 118575_2nd and 118577_2nd: 6 min
  - cut 5 U windows: 18 min
  - patches for 4 new training halves: 32 min
  - re-cut for negatives or new frames: up to 40 min
- **P1, F and U, 4.5 h:**
  - 2 variants of 60 min training each
  - U eval: COCO once, 0.6 h; 1 h per variant for 4 checkpoints
  - S1 judging: about 45 min of agent time
  - G1' decided
- **P2, V detector, 2.5 h:**
  - GSR for 117093_2nd and 132877_2nd: 6 min
  - cut 8 V-new windows: 28 min
  - v2, v1 and COCO on the 8 windows: 1.9 h
  - v2 on V-old: 10 min

results.evaluation:
**FF-auto, frozen now.**
- **Definition:** a frame is a hit when the top-1 candidate (none = miss) has its ground point (v + size/2 through st.image_to_pitch):
  - within 4.0 m of the segment from passer (at the kick) to receiver (at reception);
  - with projection t in [0,1];
  - with |t - s| <= 0.30, s = 0.25, 0.417, 0.583, 0.75 for the 4 frames;
  - at least 1.0 m from every GSR person.
  - A pass scores the mean over its 4 frames.
- **How it was chosen, on T judgements only:**
  - Grid: W 1-5 m × pixel term 0-30 px × R 0-2 m × t-range.
  - Rule: the corridor with the lowest chance-hit rate within 0.05 of the best T kappa. It picks W 4.0 m, no pixel term, R 1.0, t in [0,1]; 1.9% of random pitch points hit it.
  - The |t - s| guard was then added against a detector trained on pass-line bags. It costs T kappa 0.84 → 0.82.
- **Agreement:**
  - T, 112 detector tiles at pass frames: kappa 0.82; 69 of 69 auto hits confirmed; 69 of 78 confirmed balls caught.
  - V-old, 97 tiles: kappa 0.81; 55 of 58 confirmed; 55 of 61 caught.
  - Decoys counted as hits: 0 of 65.
  - The registered 1 m rule: kappa 0.24 on T, 0.33 on V; it catches 0.35 and 0.43 of confirmed balls.
- **Per detector:**
  - On T it understates v1 (auto 0.62 against judged 0.74; COCO 0.61 against 0.65), which is conservative for the heatmap.
  - On V-old: 0.58 against 0.60, and 0.62 against 0.67.
- **On the existing data:**
  - T: v1 0.65 against COCO 0.50, difference +0.15 [0.09, 0.21].
  - V-old: 0.53 against 0.50, difference +0.03 [-0.07, 0.14].
  - This reproduces the blind ranking and shows T flattering v1.
- **Disclosure:** the V-old kappas were seen during this design, so V-new tiles are the clean check.

**Detector family (alpha 0.025 two-sided, fixed sequence):**
- **H1, v2 better than COCO in free flight on V** (V-old plus V-new, about 200 passes).
  - Test: paired FF-auto difference, bootstrap over 1-minute blocks, 4,000 draws. Reject when the lower bound of the 97.5% interval is above 0.
  - Validity conditions, on the V-new blind tiles:
    - per-detector kappa of FF-auto against the judge at least 0.6;
    - differential bias (auto minus judged for v2, minus the same for COCO) at most +0.05;
    - decoys judged ball at most 1.
  - If any validity condition fails, the declared fallback primary is the exact McNemar test on the 100 judged passes: p < 0.025 with more v2-only hits.
- **"Clearly better than COCO"** (the user's goal) needs all of:
  - H1 rejected;
  - FF-auto difference at least +0.10;
  - blind difference at least +0.10;
  - the same sign on M2 and on M10 separately.
- **H2, v2 better than v1:** FF-auto on all V passes, same rule. Tested only if H1 is rejected.

**Secondary (descriptive, intervals only):**
- blind McNemar p;
- legacy 1 m hit;
- feet share;
- action hit against a random point;
- confident-pick precision (40 v2 tiles at p >= tau) against v1's 32/40;
- candidates per frame;
- old V against V-new;
- the gap between T, U and V;
- blind v2 against v1 on V-old's 38 passes.

**Power:**
- FF-auto: SD of the per-pass difference is 0.33. With about 200 passes and design effect 1.3, SE is about 0.027 and the 80% MDE at alpha 0.025 is about 0.08. A +0.14 gain gives power above 0.99.
- Blind on 100 passes (simulated): power 0.66 at +0.14 and 0.93 at +0.20 at alpha 0.025.

**Blind tiles: about 425 in 4 sittings of about 105.** Sources hidden, shuffled, about 20% decoys, keys and FF-auto opened only after judging. Categories B / B* / S / N, hit = B.
- **S1, on U before V:**
  - 60 v2 top-1 tiles at one frame per U pass
  - 20 v2 confident picks
  - 20 decoys
  - It must show FF-auto kappa at least 0.6 and at least 0.85 of v2's auto hits confirmed.
- **S2 and S3:** 100 V-new passes (random, seed 3); for each, v2 and COCO top-1 at q=1, plus 25 decoys. About 215 tiles.
- **S4:**
  - v2 at V-old's 38 passes
  - 12 old tiles re-judged as a drift check (at least 11 of 12 should agree; earlier re-judging gave 15 of 16)
  - 40 v2 confident picks on V-new random frames
  - about 20 decoys

**Gate G1' on U, before anything runs on V.**
- All of:
  - FF-auto v2 minus COCO at least +0.10 with 95% lower bound above 0;
  - S1 validity met;
  - confident precision at least 0.75.
- On failure: iterate the recipe on U (at most 4 variants, all reported). If it still fails, there is no flight claim, and events continue with the detector that does best on U.

**Old-V comparability:** same windows, frames and code, with the reused judgements. Old-V and V-new rows are reported separately and pooled.

**Variant cap:** v1 is variant 1 on V and F is variant 2; the third stays in reserve. Fold detectors, U variants, and COCO or v1 reruns do not count.
results.events_plan:
Events start only after F and tau are frozen and the V detector results are recorded. No event-tuning window's match is in its ball detector's training data.

1. **Out-of-fold balls.** Folds A and B (frozen recipe) produce balls on the 4 E-tune windows: A for M6 and M8, B for M3 and M4.
   - Fold-equivalence check: fold FF-auto and action hit on their held-out E-tune windows against F on U.
   - A gap above 0.10 is disclosed: the rules would then be tuned for a weaker ball.
2. **Configurations:**
   - C0: COCO ball with v1 rules (cached)
   - C1: v1 heatmap with v1 rules (V-old only, for continuity)
   - C2: v2 ball with v1 rules
   - C3: v2 ball with retuned rules
3. **Sweep** (sweep_events_v2.py on cached tracks with balls swapped in; it overrides module constants as the existing sweep_*.py do). Staged, pre-registered, about 85 settings:
   - **A, ball input:** top-k {1, 2, 4} × tau at {1, 0.5, 2} candidates per frame.
   - **B, possession:** POSSESSION_RADIUS_M {2, 3, 4, 8} × MIN_POSSESSION_HOLD_S {0.2, 0.4, 0.6} × POSSESSION_GAP_FILL_S {0.5, 1.5, 3.0}.
   - **C, pass and carry:** MIN_PASS_DISTANCE_M {0.3, 2, 4} × CARRY_MIN_TIME_S {0.8, 1.2, 1.6} × CARRY_MIN_DISTANCE_M {0, 2}.
   - **D, shots, by rate:** too few labels for F1. SHOT_MIN_KMH {10, 30, 50, 70} × SHOT_MAX_DIST_FROM_GOAL_M {50, 30, 20}: the most permissive setting giving at most 1.5 × shot labels + 2 pooled.
   - Then re-check stage A with B to D fixed.
   - Receiver, tackle and out rules stay at v1.
   - **Objective:** pooled pass+carry F1 at 1 s over E-tune.
     - Within 0.01 of the best: fewest parameters changed from v1, then fewest events.
     - Constraint: pass+carry events between 0.6 and 1.5 × labels in every window (v1 with the heatmap ball fired 3×).
   - Optimism is reported by leave-one-window-out: choose on 3 windows, score the 4th.
4. **Gate G-E, before V.**
   - Retuned rules must pass both:
     - leave-one-window-out mean F1 at least that of v1 rules on the same fold balls + 0.02;
     - on E-check (2 M5 windows, F's balls), F1 at least v1 rules' and count ratio at most 1.5.
   - On failure: one disclosed retry on E-tune only; otherwise freeze v1 rules (C3 = C2, H4 dropped).
5. **Freeze.** The settings JSON and its hash go into the protocol before any V event is computed.
   - The V-new player pipeline may run earlier, since it does not depend on v2.
   - Its events.json (COCO with v1 rules) stays unopened until the freeze.
6. **V events, 4 windows, about 260 pass+carry labels.** Events family at alpha 0.025, fixed sequence:
   - **H3, C3 better than C0:** pooled pass+carry F1 at 1 s, 10 s block bootstrap; the lower bound of the 97.5% interval must be above 0.
   - **H4, C3 better than C2:** the retune's own effect. Tested only if H3 is rejected.
   - Descriptive:
     - per-window F1 against chance F1, with p;
     - excess over chance;
     - tolerances 0.5 and 2 s;
     - ball near the actor;
     - team and actor right;
     - shots, won and out counts against labels;
     - C1.
   - MDE is about 0.13 F1, stated in advance, so a smaller gain will read as not shown.
results.expected_effect:
**Measurement:**
- FF-auto agrees with the blind judge at kappa about 0.8, against 0.24-0.33 for the registered 1 m rule.
- It uses about 200 V passes instead of 38. The MDE falls from about 0.15 to about 0.08 (alpha 0.025).
- Tuning on an unseen match (M5) removes the T flattering seen in v1.

**Detector:**
- If v2 really gains about +0.14 over COCO in flight, the design detects it: FF-auto power above 0.99, blind power 0.66 at alpha 0.025.
- If v2 is no better, as v1 was, G1' on U stops it before V and the V variant is not spent.

**Events:**
- Tuning is free of leakage: balls come from detectors that never saw the tuning match, and the rules are frozen before V.
- Expected: over-firing cut from about 3× to at most 1.5× labels, and false shots from 182 to roughly 10.
- A pass+carry F1 gain of about 0.13 or more over the COCO system would be shown; smaller gains would be reported as not shown.
risks: U is a single match (M5): the lowest pass rate (4.2/min) and only about 78 passes, so the MDE on U is about 0.15 and tuning choices may fit M5. Mitigated by at most 4 variants and the T seen-match diagnostic.

FF-auto was checked only against the failure modes of v1 and COCO. A v2 trained with pass-line bags could fire along the corridor without finding the ball. Defences: the timing guard |t - s| <= 0.3, the 1 m clearance from players, the v2-specific blind checks (S1 on U, S2-S3 on V-new), the differential-bias rule, and the declared blind fallback.

FF-auto misses confirmed balls more than 4 m off the passer-receiver line (deflections, GSR or label error) or within 1 m of a player. It catches about 0.88-0.90 of confirmed balls and undercounted v1 on T by 0.12. That is conservative, but absolute rates are low.
This design looked at the V-old kappas over the whole grid. The tolerance was chosen on T by a stated rule, but V-old is no longer a clean check of FF-auto; only the V-new tiles are.
V has only two matches (M2, M10), from the same rigs and league. 'Unseen matches' rests on n=2, hence the requirement of the same sign on each match. M7 and M9 stay untouched.
One judge, who knows the hypothesis. About 425 tiles cause fatigue; mitigated by hidden sources, decoys, the re-judging drift check and 4 sittings.

Event rules are tuned on fold balls (detectors trained on 3 matches) but deployed with F (4 matches), so calibration and quality differ. Mitigated by label-free per-detector tau, the fold-equivalence check and the E-check on M5 (which reuses U windows, so it is slightly optimistic).

Events power is limited: about 260 V labels give an MDE of about 0.13 F1. Shots, won and out have too few labels to tune or claim, and team errors on M2 (accuracy about 0.5) cap event F1 whatever the ball.
Splitting alpha 0.025 per family costs power. With fixed-sequence testing, H2 and H4 go untested if H1 or H3 fail.
About 23 h of compute on a shared 4-core box will likely overrun. The cut order (E-check, then the second variant, then V-new windows 4 to 3 per match) must be declared before any V run.
