best_ideas: The biggest lever for a 5-15 px ball on a FIXED panorama is time, not labels. Frame differences (t-2, t+2) plus a 28 s running-median background make a moving ball-sized blob stand out. They also make the static distractors that cost v1 and COCO on unseen matches vanish from the F channel: penalty spots, lines, balls resting by a goal, stand furniture. These cues depend less on each match's grass texture and lighting than RGB does, and RGB-only v1 lost a lot from T to V (blind 0.75 to 0.50).

The motion stem starts at zero and is added before bn1, so step 0 is exactly v1's ImageNet start. Motion dropout (p 0.1) keeps the detector working on a resting ball at set pieces, and temporal reversal doubles the motion examples. The claimed cost is low: +7% inference and +18% per training step, from a benchmark. The probe found 1.6% of pitch pixels above 25 against the background, so background subtraction is clean on this footage.
A no-motion ablation on the same labels, measured on the tuning match only. It shows whether labels or motion did the work, and it is a ready fallback if the strip pipeline goes wrong.

A linker in pitch metres with Jacobian measurement noise. I checked this: score_soccernet.py calls ball_selection.select_single_ball with a single px_per_m from estimate_px_per_m, on a view that spans about 2 to 72 px/m. On saved v1 candidates I reproduced the re-ranking headroom on V: top-1 in the corridor 0.49, any of top-3 0.66, any of 8 0.70 (COCO 0.47 / 0.51 / 0.53). Events need one correct ball per frame, so this is also the most useful events fix.

M6 as the held-out tuning match. It has more passes than M5 (310/249 per half against 202). It has the resting-ball distractor (11 of COCO's 17 M6 pass tiles were B*), like M2's penalty spots. One M6 window already has a cached player pipeline, and the old M6 judgements can be reused.

A constant-velocity blob miner that turns a corridor bag into a 0.4 m point label, used only if a blind check (S1) finds at least 90% of its picks are the match ball. This is the only route in any design to strong labels for the ball in flight.
flaws: The corridor labels are coarser than in the labels design. Passer and receiver are ignored instead of being hard negatives, so feet stay in the bag. Feet are about half of v1's wrong V picks: I counted 10 of 21 within 2 m of a player. The bag is a 3 m band with a 2 m chip extension upwards (about 144 px on the near side). With 256 px crops most near-side corridor bags are dropped.

About 16 h of compute. There are many new parts: a strip builder with a 14 s delayed background queue, the miner, the 12-channel stem, a Kalman+Viterbi linker and an events tuner. The evaluation needs dense stride-2 inference (t+-2 frames and the background). The bug and overrun risk is the highest of the three designs.
Strips are stored as JPEG q95 crops, so the frame differences carry block noise. At inference they come from H.264 frames, a train/test mismatch for 4 px balls.
Far-side balls moving in depth shift only about 1.7 px in 2 frames, and the 28 s median absorbs dead balls; the background channel has to carry those cases.

The corridor-3m measure has no timing guard and no placebo test against a model that fires on the empty grass between team-mates. On the tuning match, gate G2 asks for exact McNemar p < 0.05 on about 60 passes, so a real +0.15 gain could still stop the run.

best_ideas: The corridor geometry is measured on judged balls. I re-derived it from tiles_ff_geometry.csv: the perpendicular distance has median 1.1-1.2 m and 90th percentile 3.2 m. 98% of the balls are at least 1 m from every player; the far side is larger in metres than in pixels. The bag is the union of a metric rule and a pixel rule, centred on a decelerating-ball time t_hat with a window of -0.22 to +0.28, plus an upward extension for height.
The body box of every player outside the bag is a hard negative, passer and receiver included, and this overrides ignore. That attacks v1's feet failure directly.

Free patches target where v1 actually failed on V. Several of its wrong V picks were near-touchline or stand objects, ground y above 31 m and 15 m or more from any player. The design adds a touchline/goal-line strip, landmark disks (penalty spots), about 6,000 free patches against v1's 724, and ignore disks around COCO-detected spare balls so that a real resting ball is never labelled 'not a ball'.
320 px patches, so the near-side corridor bags fit in the patch.
The size-invariant LSE pool and BCE on the 16 strongest negative peaks. Both answer v1's broad, badly calibrated activations (8 candidates per frame at tau <= 0.15).
A Platt fit on the held-out match, so tau means something.
A placebo measure at frames before the kick: a direct test for a learned prior on the line between team-mates. Corridor decoys in the blind tiles do the same for the judge.
The most compute-realistic plan (about 8.5 h), built mostly on the existing code paths.
flaws: The detector stays single-frame RGB. Nothing addresses the unseen-match appearance shift that sank v1 (T 0.75 to V 0.50 blind) or v1's recall ceiling: 30% of V free-flight frames had no v1 candidate in the corridor among 8. On a static camera this leaves the strongest available cue unused.
Many loss changes arrive at once: ranking with a null option, peak suppression, the new pool, scale jitter and blur, plus pseudo-label variant B. None is ablated, so a failure cannot be diagnosed.

The automatic measure is the training bag's own geometry (2.5 m | 20 px), and checkpoints are chosen by it. Only the placebo stands against self-confirmation. My random-point check gives it a chance-hit rate of 1.4-2.1% against 0.9-1.7% for the protocol's 4 m + |t-s| rule.
The tuning match U = M5 has the lowest pass rate (about 4.2/min), so its decisions are noisy. The V blind primary has 38 passes, which the design itself calls about a coin flip.
The events plan needs player pipeline runs on the M5 windows, which are not cached and not counted in the 8.5 h. It keeps select_single_ball and its single px_per_m on the panorama.

best_ideas: FF-auto is chosen on the T judgements by a stated rule: 4 m from the pass segment, a timing guard |t-s| <= 0.3, at least 1 m from every player. It agrees with the judge at kappa 0.82 on T and 0.81 on old V, against 0.24/0.33 for the registered 1 m rule. On random points its chance-hit rate is the lowest of the three corridor measures; I re-checked it at 0.9-1.7%.

V grows by fixed rule to about 200 passes, from fresh M2/M10 minutes cut only after the detector is frozen. The detectable difference falls to about 0.08. Automatic summaries stay sealed until the blind judging is recorded.

Validity conditions are checked on v2's OWN blind tiles: per-detector kappa, differential bias against COCO, decoys. Blind McNemar is declared in advance as the fallback primary. 'Clearly better' also needs the same sign on M2 and on M10 separately.
Provenance JSON with every checkpoint, and a leakage guard that refuses windows from training matches. Guard bands of +-60 s keep the old T windows usable as a seen-match diagnostic.
Two alpha families (detector, events) with a fixed order of tests. The ball-swap tooling moves into the repo, so every event configuration shares identical players and teams.
flaws: It brings no detector improvement of its own and defers the recipe to the label design. It forbids a temporal tracker, which gives up the 0.49 to 0.66 re-ranking headroom I verified and leaves the single px_per_m in select_single_ball wrong for events.

Fold detectors A and B for leak-free event tuning cost about 4.5 h (two trainings plus inference). Trained on 3 matches, they give weaker balls than the final detector F. Tuning on a held-out match with F's own balls is also leak-free and cheaper.
About 23 h of CPU on a shared 4-core box, and about 425 blind tiles in 4 sittings. The overrun and judge-fatigue risk is high.
Its U = M5 is the lowest-pass match: about 78 passes over 6 windows.

results.recommended_combination:
Put the motion design's input on top of the labels design's labels. Measure them with the protocol design's validated measure. Then tune events on one held-out match. Budget: about 13-15 h of CPU.

(1) SPLIT
- Train F on both halves of M3, M4, M5 and M8. Use +-60 s guard bands from the protocol design.
- Hold out M6 entirely as the tuning match U. Reasons:
  - more passes per window than M5;
  - its resting-ball distractor mirrors M2's penalty spots;
  - one window has a cached player pipeline;
  - the old M6 judgements can be reused.
- Add provenance JSON per checkpoint and a leakage guard (protocol design).

(2) LABELS (labels design)
- Corridor bags:
  - the union of 2.5 m and 20 px around passer->receiver;
  - centred on t_hat = s + 0.4 s(1-s), window -0.22 to +0.28;
  - extended upwards by 1 m x sx;
  - player cells inside the bag set to ignore.
- Every body outside the bag is a hard negative, passer and receiver included.
- Lofted passes get negatives outside a height curtain only.
- About 6,000 free patches: player clusters, landmarks, a touchline/goal-line strip, random. COCO-detected spare balls get ignore disks.
- Patches of 320 px.

(3) INPUT AND MODEL (motion design)
- Each sample stores t-2, t, t+2 and a 28 s running-median background crop.
- The zero-initialised 9-channel motion conv is summed into the ImageNet stem.
- Motion dropout 0.1 and temporal reversal.
- Store the crops at q98, or as PNG for the t+-2 crops, to limit difference noise. Disk is about 7-8 GB, which fits.

(4) LOSS
- v1's MIL and focal loss, plus the labels design's size-invariant LSE pool and suppression of the top-16 negative peaks.
- Leave out, until U shows a need: the ranking/null term, pseudo-label variant B, and the blob miner. The miner can be added later behind its S1 blind gate.
- 5,000 steps (about 1.8 h).
- One no-motion run on the same labels (about 1.5 h), scored on U only. It shows whether motion or labels did the work, and it is the fallback.

(5) INFERENCE
- detect_v2 with the background.
- Platt calibration and tau fitted on U.
- The motion design's pitch-metre Viterbi linker:
  - always used for events (it replaces select_single_ball's single px_per_m on the calibrated path);
  - used for the detector's top-1 pick only if it adds at least +0.03 on U (registered rule);
  - raw top-1 always reported.
- For U and V scoring, run the net only at measured frames and their t+-2 neighbours, reading the video sequentially. Dense stride 2 runs only on the events windows.

(6) MEASUREMENT
- Automatic measure: the protocol design's FF-auto, frozen now (4 m, |t-s| <= 0.3, >= 1 m from players).
- Line-prior checks: the labels design's placebo frames (gate <= 0.05) and corridor decoys in every blind set.
- Gate G on U before anything runs on V: FF-auto v2 - COCO >= 0.10 with lower bound > 0, placebo <= 0.05, and a blind U check (about 110 tiles) with FF-auto kappa >= 0.6 on v2's own picks.
- V extension: fresh M2/M10 windows registered now and cut after the freeze. Protocol design's rule, trimmed to 3 per match: about 140-150 passes in total.
- V primary: FF-auto paired bootstrap over 1-minute blocks, plus the protocol design's validity conditions and declared blind-McNemar fallback.
- Blind V tiles: one frame per pass for about 100 passes, v2/v1/COCO deduplicated, about 20% decoys, sealed until judged, about 2 sittings.
- 'Clearly better than COCO' needs the same sign on M2 and on M10.
- This spends V variant 2 of 3.

(7) EVENTS
- Tune on 2-3 M6 windows with v2's linked ball: reuse the cached M6 first-half pipeline and run 1-2 more pipelines. No fold detectors.
- Use the protocol design's ball-swap sweep tool moved into the repo.
- Parameters: the motion design's six (possession radius, hold, max ball speed, carry time, pass distance), plus a shot gate on distance to goal and on the velocity pointing into the goal mouth.
- Objective: pass+carry F1 minus chance at 1 s, with events between 0.6 and 1.5 x labels per window, and the plateau/simplest choice.
- Report leave-one-window-out; freeze; run once on 4 V windows (about 260 labels).
- Report C3 (v2 + retuned) against C0 (COCO + v1 rules), with C2 (v2 + v1 rules) as the decomposition.

Cut order if time runs short, declared before V:
1. the no-motion ablation;
2. the third V-extension window per match;
3. the second U events window.

best_ideas: Corridor bags built from measured in-flight geometry. I re-derived it from design_splits/tiles_ff_geometry.csv: 51 unique confirmed balls on T, perpendicular median 1.12 m, 90th percentile 3.2 m; t-s median +0.08, 5-95% [-0.19, +0.32]. The bags are centred on a decelerating t_hat instead of v1's constant-speed point, which covers only about 49% of these balls.
Every player body more than 1 m outside the bag is a hard negative in flight frames. This targets the main v1 error: on T, 11 of 16 wrong v1 tiles were within 2 m of a player, and 10 of 21 on V.

About 6,000 ball-free patches with landmark hard negatives (penalty spots, spots, corners). Off-landmark COCO detections become ignore regions rather than negatives, so a spare or resting ball is not labelled 'not a ball'.
A placebo measure: the same corridor rule at frames before the kick. With it, corridor decoys in the blind tiles test whether the judge is biased toward expected ball positions inside the corridor.
The automatic measure gets a v2-specific blind precision check on U (G2(3)), with demotion if precision is below 0.9. A Platt fit only sets tau and leaves the top-1 ranking unchanged.
M5 is held out as an unseen tuning match. v1 trained on M5's first half, so U is conservative against v1.
flaws: The primary claim is a blind McNemar test on V-old's 38 passes. By the design's own estimate it is about a coin flip even at +0.12-0.15. The power of the co-primary is overstated: n=113 with SD 0.33 and design effect ~1.3 gives SE ~0.035 and an MDE of ~0.10, not 0.08.

V-old judgements shaped the label constants: the far/near-side medians and the pixel term were 'pooled T+V'. V-old's 38 passes are then the primary blind set and part of the co-primary. This leak is mild but undisclosed. Recomputed on V, the 2.5 m|20 px rule has precision 0.92 and kappa 0.73, against T's 0.97 and 0.81.
The automatic corridor measure has no timing guard (|t-s|), so it accepts any point along the whole 16 m segment.

The 'size-invariant' bag pool is not size-invariant. Unnormalised LSE with r=4 adds log(N)/4 (~1.4 logits for N≈1000 cells), so broad, low activation over the corridor satisfies the bag. The softmax ranking term is also satisfied by broad bag mass. Only negatives outside the bag and the peakiness monitor push toward a single peak.
Patch jitter drops to ±48 px on 320 px patches, so the bag always sits near the patch centre (centre prior through padding). It should be at least ±100 px or a random crop.
The events comparison has no rule-versus-ball decomposition: there is no COCO + retuned rules and no v2 + old rules. The retune alone (cutting 3x over-firing) could produce the F1 gain.

Compute is understated at 8.5 h. No player pipeline exists for any M5 window (I checked: output_st2_* covers only M2, M3, M4-1st, M6-1st, M8-1st and M10), so the U events retune needs 2 uncosted runs (~2-2.5 h). The V-ext evaluation of 3 detectors on 4 windows, 5 U checkpoints plus v1 and COCO, and blind sittings put a realistic total near 12-14 h.
Variant B (pseudo-label shrinking) and the extra loss terms add untested moving parts to a single seed.

best_ideas: Motion input: signed differences to t±2 plus a 28 s running-median background, through a zero-initialised 9-channel stem summed into the ImageNet stem, so training starts exactly at v1. Motion is the strongest known cue for 4-6 px far-side balls and transfers across matches better than appearance. The background directly removes static distractors: M2 penalty spots and resting balls by goals.
A same-loader --no-motion ablation separates the motion effect from the label effect without spending a V variant.

A ball linker in pitch metres with Jacobian measurement noise. I verified in score_soccernet.py lines 425-426 that select_single_ball runs on a single px_per_m scale, while this panorama spans about 2-72 px/m. The defect is real and matters for events.
Re-ranking headroom is measured (v1 on V: top-1 0.49, any of top-3 0.66), so linking has something to recover.
The events plan has a proper decomposition (v2 + current rules, COCO + retuned rules), an F1-minus-chance objective, a plateau rule and leave-one-window-out stability.
Judge drift is checked with re-judged old tiles, and all old V tiles are re-judged if agreement falls below 0.9.
flaws: The primary V claim compares v2's linked pick with COCO's raw top-1. That mixes the detector effect with the tracker effect. The primary should use raw top-1 for every detector, or link all of them.
The linker uses the pipeline's player detections, so the detector's primary result depends on the player pipeline, and pipeline runs are needed on the V windows just to score the ball.

M6 was picked as the tuning match because COCO fails there on resting balls, a choice informed by V's penalty-spot failure. The S2/G2 margins over COCO are therefore inflated by selection. V stays clean, but the gates are less informative.

corridor-3m was validated on T and V-old judgements pooled (162 tiles), so V-old is not a clean check of it. The measure has no |t-s| guard, and 2 of 65 decoys counted as automatic hits in my recomputation.
The blind G2 gate needs McNemar p<0.05 on about 60 T2 passes, which is underpowered. Up to two further T2 iterations then invite overfitting to M6.
The V blind primary has about 76 passes with Holm over 2 comparisons, so only a gain of about +0.2 is likely to pass.

There is a train/test noise mismatch. Strips are q95 JPEG (difference channels carry JPEG block artefacts), while inference uses H.264 frames. A 4 px ball's difference signal is fragile; lossless strips or q98 fit the 24 GB disk.

There are many new components at once: strip extraction with a delayed queue, the background, the blob miner plus an S1 blind gate of 100 tiles, Kalman+Viterbi, the events tuner and pipeline changes. 16 h is optimistic, and 20-24 h of wall time on the shared box is more likely.
The background absorbs any ball still for more than about 14 s, so FREE KICK bags are dropped. Restarts are lost for events.

best_ideas: The automatic free-flight measure (4 m, |t-s|<=0.3, >=1 m from every person) was chosen on T judgements only, by a stated rule. Recomputed from tiles_ff_geometry.csv: T kappa 0.82 and V kappa 0.79, 0 of 65 decoys counted as automatic hits, chance about 1.9%. For comparison, the registered 1 m rule has kappa 0.22/0.33 and recall 0.34/0.42.

Validity is checked per detector on clean V-new blind tiles: kappa >= 0.6, differential bias (v2 minus COCO) <= 0.05, decoys. A blind McNemar fallback is declared in advance, automatic results stay sealed until judging is done, and the old V.json must be reproduced as a regression check first.

Power comes from about 200 V passes in windows fixed now by rule and cut only after the freeze. The MDE is about 0.08 at alpha 0.025; I verified 0.33/sqrt(200)·sqrt(1.3)·3.08 ≈ 0.082. 'Clearly better' needs the same sign on M2 and on M10 separately, which honestly reflects that V is only 2 matches.

Leakage engineering: provenance JSON for each checkpoint, a hard assert that no patch comes from U, V, test or M1, guard bands around the old T windows (which keeps a seen-match gap diagnostic), and two alpha families with fixed-sequence testing.

Events are tuned on out-of-fold balls, using cached player pipelines and balls from detectors that never saw that match. The C0/C2/C3 decomposition separates the ball effect from the rules effect, and the MDE (about 0.13 F1) is stated in advance.
flaws: There is no detector recipe of its own. Any free-flight gain depends entirely on the label or motion design it is paired with.

23 h of CPU time on a shared 4-core box. The two fold detectors (about 2 h of training plus 2.5 h of inference) buy leakage-free events tuning that could be had more cheaply: tune on M5 windows with F's balls, since M5 is already out-of-sample for F.
Fold detectors train on 3 matches and F on 4, so the rules are tuned for a weaker ball. The design acknowledges this; the equivalence check only discloses it.

V-old kappas were inspected across the whole tolerance grid (disclosed). Which primary applies (automatic or blind fallback) is decided by validity data from V itself; this is pre-declared but data-dependent.

About 425 blind tiles from one judge who knows the hypothesis invites fatigue. Corridor decoys, which test bias toward expected positions, are not specified; decoys are random pitch points that are easy to reject.
'No temporal tracker in v2' also keeps the single-scale select_single_ball defect for events, even though a metric-space selection could be an events-side setting frozen before V.

results.recommended_combination:
Base the plan on the 'protocol' design's splits and measurement, the 'labels' design's label recipe, and the 'motion' design's input as a second variant on U. Keep each design's add-ons only where they do not mix effects.

(1) Splits and leakage, from 'protocol'.
- F trains on both halves of M3, M4, M6 and M8. The old T windows are excluded with ±1 min guard bands; T stays a seen-match diagnostic only.
- M5 is U: about 6 windows, the only place where choices are made.
- Each checkpoint stores its provenance, and scripts assert that no patch comes from U, V, test or M1.
- V-new: 6-8 windows of M2 and M10 fixed now by rule (about 150-200 passes in total with V-old), cut only after F and tau are frozen.
- Before v2 is scored, a regression run must reproduce V.json exactly.

(2) Measurement.
- Freeze FF-auto now: 4 m corridor, |t-s| <= 0.3, at least 1 m from every person, chosen on T only.
- Write its results to a sealed file, opened only after the blind sittings are judged.
- Primary: the paired difference over V-old plus V-new, block bootstrap, alpha 0.025.
- Validity on clean V-new blind tiles, per detector: kappa >= 0.6 and differential bias <= 0.05, with the declared blind-McNemar fallback.
- "Clearly better" also requires the same sign on M2 and on M10.
- From 'labels': add the pre-kick placebo (reported for v1 and COCO as the reference level) and corridor decoys to every blind sitting.
- Score every detector, v2 included, by raw top-1. A linker never enters the detector claim.

(3) Recipe, from 'labels'.
- Corridor bags centred on the decelerating t_hat.
- Player bodies more than 1 m outside the bag as hard negatives.
- About 6,000 ball-free patches with landmark negatives; off-landmark COCO balls set to ignore.
- Changes to the 'labels' version:
  - keep v1's log-mean-exp bag pool, or monitor peakiness, because the 'size-invariant' unnormalised LSE rewards broad corridor activation;
  - widen jitter to at least ±100 px;
  - Platt fit only to set tau;
  - leave out the ranking/null term and pseudo-label variant B at first.

(4) Motion, from 'motion', as U variant B.
- Cut strips [t-2 | t | t+2 | background] once, lossless or q98, with JPEG augmentation that matches.
- Variant A is the same loader with --no-motion (RGB only); variant B uses the zero-initialised motion stem. Labels and steps are identical, so this is a clean ablation.
- Pre-registered rule: B goes to V only if it beats A on U FF-auto by >= 0.03 and passes the U blind check (S1); otherwise A goes.
- Only one V variant is spent (the 2nd of 3).
- Drop the blob-miner labels and self-training from the base plan.

(5) Events, after the detector and its V results are frozen.
- Tune on M5 windows with F's balls. F never saw M5, so this is out-of-sample, and the U windows are already cut. Run the player pipeline on 2-3 M5 windows (about 150-230 pass+carry labels).
- Skip fold detectors unless compute is spare.
- Grid (coarse, with a plateau rule):
  - possession radius and hold;
  - carry time;
  - shot gate (speed, distance to goal, direction into the goal mouth);
  - candidates per frame (top-k) and tau;
  - ball selection in pitch metres, using the motion design's linker, or select_single_ball fed metric coordinates; this fixes the verified single-px_per_m defect.
- Objective: pooled pass+carry F1 minus chance F1. Constraints: count 0.6-1.5x labels, shots bounded. Report leave-one-window-out.
- Report C0 (COCO, old rules), C2 (v2, old rules), C3 (v2, retuned) and COCO with retuned rules, on about 4 V windows (about 260 labels).
- Claim an events gain only if the lower bound is above 0 (MDE about 0.13, stated in advance).

Budget: about 18-20 h of CPU, with this cut order declared before any V run: V-new 8→6 windows, then the motion variant, then the third M5 events window.

Build the strips and labels.

build_ball_patches.py writes one 1280x320 JPEG q98 per sample: [t-2 | t | t+2 | B(t)].
- Kinds: flight, lofted, action, dribble, free.
- Slack-aware jitter up to ±100 px.
- Samples are queued until frame c+350 is decoded (a 15-frame deque of full frames, about 200 MB).

Run 8 halves, two at a time: 118575 1+2, 118576 1+2, 118577 1+2, 128058 1+2. The 2nd halves of 118576 and 128058 skip frames 13,500-20,999.

- adds corridor(), curtain(), landmark_cells(), free_codes() and a COCO ignore pass (yolov8s, conf >= 0.25, t crop upsampled x2);
- writes labels.parquet and labels_codes.npy (80x80 int8);

At the same time, run the player pipeline once on st2_118578_2nd_f015000 (as for events_v1: COCO ball, teams, calibrated). It becomes the second events tuning window.

U baselines.

- COCO on all U measured frames (pass, placebo, PASS/DRIVE, random) of the 5 M6 windows.
- v1 (ball_heatmap.3000.pt) on U pass and placebo frames.
- Save as U_base.json in the scratchpad.

Train v2 with the motion stem: train_ball_heatmap.py --motion.

- Strip loader: one JPEG split into 4 crops.
- MIX and loss as in training_spec. LR groups: conv1_motion trains from step 1; the RGB stem and layer1 are frozen to step 800.

U selection and calibration.

One decode per U window runs all 3 checkpoints on pass and placebo frames.
- Choose the checkpoint with the highest U FF-auto; within 0.02, the later one.
- Run the chosen checkpoint on all U frames (top-8 with logits), plus the motion-zeroed diagnostic (motion channels set to 0) on pass and placebo frames.
- T diagnostic (--allow-seen) on st2_118576_2nd_f015000 and st2_128058_2nd_f015000.

calibrate_ball_heatmap.py (new):
- Platt (a, b) on U candidate logits. Positives: FF-auto geometry at pass frames; within 1.5 m of the actor at PASS/DRIVE frames.
- Writes <ckpt>.calib.json with a, b, a reliability table, and tau = the smallest p_cal giving <= 1.0 candidates per frame on U random frames.

Compute G1 and G2. The detector is now frozen: checkpoint, a, b, tau.

Blind sitting S1 on U, then G3.

S1 has about 110 tiles:
- v2 top-1 at q=1 per U pass (about 74);
- 12 confident v2 picks;
- 12 random and 12 corridor decoys.

The sealed FF-auto is opened only after the sitting is judged. Decide G. If G fails, run the RGB-only fallback (step 6 --no-motion, then step 7) once.

Meanwhile, network-bound: stream the GSR of 117093_2nd and 132877_2nd, and cut the 6 V-new windows: st2_117093_1st_f045000, st2_117093_2nd_f015000, st2_117093_2nd_f045000, st2_132877_1st_f045000, st2_132877_2nd_f015000, st2_132877_2nd_f045000.

- v1 and COCO at the V-old placebo frames.
- Results are written with --sealed.
- Build S2 tiles: 50 V-new passes (seed 3, 25 per match); v2 and COCO top-1 at q=1, deduped; 10 random and 10 corridor decoys.

Events.

- src/events.py: detect_events(..., params=None) temporarily overrides module constants; new SHOT_MOUTH_MARGIN_M (None = v1) in _toward_goal; a FIXED_VIEW_V3 profile, filled after the freeze.

- sweep_events_v2.py (new): the staged grid on U-E; writes events_v3.json and its sha256.

results.label_spec:
STRIPS (build_ball_patches.py)

Each sample is one JPEG at q98, 1280x320, holding [t-2 | t | t+2 | B(t)]: four 320 px crops at the same (x0, y0).
- B(t) is the per-pixel median of 15 frames at 50-frame spacing, centred on c = 125*round(t/125). It is clipped to the half and needs at least 8 samples. Inference uses the identical rule.
- Jitter: the crop offset on each axis is uniform in ±min(100, slack) px, with slack = (320 - bag bbox extent)/2 - 8 (at least 0). This avoids a centre prior.

Halves:
- 118575 1+2, 118576 1+2, 118577 1+2 and 128058 1+2.
- The 2nd halves of 118576 and 128058 exclude frames 13,500-20,999.
- The builder refuses 118578 (U), 117093 and 132877 (V), 117092 (M1), 128057 (M7) and 132831 (M9).

Metadata per strip: match, half, frame, kind, category, A, B, s, t_hat, L, event ids, x0, y0 and the number of background samples. 300 strips (1.5%, stratified by kind) are held out for the monitor.

CODES (build_ball_labels.py)

There is one code per 4x4 cell (80x80 int8): 1 bag, 0 ignore, -1 negative, -3 hard negative. Codes come from:
- each cell centre's ground point P = image_to_pitch(cell centre);
- the half's GSR at frame t (feet, body boxes);
- BAS actions with actors (st.with_actors), the ball track npz and the calibration.

Ball size is 0.22 m x max(sx, sy).

1. flight (about 6,400). Sources:
   - completed ground PASS: next actor a team-mate, L = |B-A| >= 10 m, >= 0.8 s, with A the passer's feet at the kick and B the receiver's at the next event;
   - intercepted PASS: next event an opponent's PASS/DRIVE/HIGH PASS 0.8-4 s later, with B the interceptor.

   Frames: s in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} + U(-0.08, 0.08), clipped to [0.17, 0.83]. The predicted fraction is t_hat = s + 0.4 s(1-s).
   - Bag (1): P projects on A->B at t in [lo, hi], with lo = max(t_hat-0.22, 2 m/L, 0.08) and hi = min(t_hat+0.28, 1-1.5 m/L, 0.95). P must also be within 2.5 m perpendicular, or the cell within 20 px of the projected sub-segment [lo, hi].
     - Add cells up to 1.0 m x sx(P) px above any bag cell (height).
     - Bag cells inside any body box, or within 1.0 m of any feet, become 0.
   - Ignore (0): the remaining cells within 6 m (ground) or 48 px (image) of the whole segment, plus a curtain 2 m x sx px above the projected segment.
   - Hard negative (-3), overriding ignore:
     - the body box of every player whose feet are >= 1.0 m from the bag's ground region, passer and receiver included;
     - landmark disks (0.75 m, at least 12 px) outside the ignore band.
   - Everything else is -1.
   - Keep the strip only if >= 85% of the bag, computed on a 640 px canvas, lies inside the crop. Otherwise retry with the window [t_hat-0.15, t_hat+0.20]; otherwise drop.
   - Provenance of the constants: T judgements (51 confirmed balls). Perpendicular distance median 1.19 m, 90th percentile 3.5 m; pixel distance median 6 px, 90th percentile 28 px; t-s median +0.10, 5-95% [-0.13, +0.41]; 96% of balls >= 1 m from every player. The near/far split was pooled with V-old (disclosed).

2. lofted (about 1,200, no positives): HIGH PASS and CROSS at s in {0.35, 0.65}.
   - The curtain is set to 0: cells above the projected segment up to clip(0.3 L, 3, 15) m x sx px, plus cells within 4 m or 32 px of the ground segment.
   - Players inside the curtain are 0, players outside are -3, the rest is -1.

3. action (about 7,000): v1's rule at every action frame with a label in v1's KEEP_ACTION, FREE KICK and THROW IN kept.
   - Bag: the region of 1.5 m around the actor's feet and the track point.
   - Other bodies and the actor's head are -3; the rest is -1.

4. dribble (about 1,200; positive-only, weight 0.5): the midpoint of gaps > 1.5 s that start with a DRIVE.
   - Bag: 1.5 m around the DRIVE actor's feet at that frame.
   - The rest is 0.
   - These replace v1's 'between' bags; the post-PASS gap bags are dropped.

5. free (about 5,200 ball-free). Two strips at every second action frame where the track status is not 0 and actor and track point agree within 3 m. Every cell's ground point must be >= 12 m from both; resample up to 10 times.
   - Centres:
     - player clusters 35% (a player with >= 2 others within 5 m);
     - landmarks 25% (penalty spots, centre spot, corners, goal posts, box and 6-yard corners, halfway/touchline crossings);
     - a boundary strip 25% (within 2 m inside a touch or goal line, or up to 60 px outside it: spare balls, ball boys);
     - random pitch points 15%.
   - Codes: -1 everywhere, bodies -3, landmark disks -3.
   - COCO sports balls (yolov8s, conf >= 0.25, on the t crop upsampled x2, i.e. full-width scale) that are not within 1 m of a landmark get a 1 m (at least 12 px) ignore disk. A real resting ball is never labelled 'not a ball'.

Expected total: about 21,000 strips, about 8.5 GB in .cache, never committed.
results.model_spec:
BallNet-M: src/ball_heatmap.build(motion=True).

The body is v1's: ResNet-18 (ImageNet) cut at stride 8 (layer2), a 1x1 lateral 128->64 upsampled and added to layer1 (stride 4), and the head [3x3 conv 64, BN, ReLU, 1x1 -> 1], with the final bias at -4.6.

The stem has two branches:
- conv1_rgb is the ImageNet conv1 (3->64, 7x7/2) on frame t, normalised with the ImageNet mean and std.
- conv1_motion (9->64, 7x7/2, no bias, weights initialised to 0) takes:
  - D- = (I_t - I_{t-2})/255/sigma_D
  - D+ = (I_t - I_{t+2})/255/sigma_D
  - F = (I_t - B(t))/255/sigma_F
  
  All are in RGB order. sigma_D and sigma_F are measured once on 1,000 training strips, stored as constants and recorded in the provenance.
- The two outputs are summed before bn1, then relu, maxpool, layer1 and layer2.

At step 0 the output equals v1's ImageNet start. Motion gradients are non-zero at once, because the motion inputs are non-zero.

When t-2 or t+2 is missing (at a window or half edge), the input is the motion-dropout one: prev = next = cur, so D is 0.

The offset of 2 frames is fixed in advance, not tuned. At stride-2 inference those frames are the neighbouring detection frames, and a pass at the median 10.5 m/s moves 16-60 px laterally between them.

build(motion=False) is v1's architecture, used for the RGB-only fallback.

Cost (synthetic benchmark):
- +7% per full-frame forward;
- +18% per training step;
- about 2.9 MB of weights.
results.inference_spec:
DETECTION. detect_v2(model, prev, cur, nxt, bg, outline, tau=0.05, top_k=8, cal):
- uses v1's crop (pitch bbox, 64 px padding above, 32 px below, padded to a multiple of 8), 5×5 local maxima, outline filter (+10 px) and sub-pixel refinement;
- returns (u, v, p_raw, size, logit), with size = 0.22 m × max(sx, sy). v1 used sx only, which is too small at the near corners.

Background: motion_bg.BackgroundCache. Pass 1 grabs every 50th frame and keeps pitch-bbox crops (about 90 × 7.6 MB per 3-minute window). B(t) uses the same 125-frame-quantised rule as training and is cached per centre.

Two paths, which must agree exactly at shared frames (checked in step 2):
1. Measured-frame path (eval_ball_detector.py --v2 CKPT[,CKPT...]): sequential decode with a 5-frame ring buffer; the net runs only at measured and placebo frames. Several checkpoints, or the motion-zeroed diagnostic, share one decode. The top-8 candidates are saved with their logits.
2. Dense path (detect_ball_heatmap.py --v2 --stride 2 --extra-frames ...): rows of tracks with confidence = p_cal, a logit column, crop_h = size and detection_method 'heatmap_v2', keeping p_raw >= 0.05 and at most 8 per frame. About 1.07× v1's cost, about 68 min per 3-minute window when two run in parallel.

CALIBRATION: p_cal = sigmoid(a·logit + b), from <ckpt>.calib.json (Platt fit on U). It does not change the ranking. tau is label-free: the smallest p_cal on the grid giving <= 1.0 candidates per frame on U random frames.

DETECTOR MEASURES: raw top-1 at any p, for every detector (v2, v1, COCO). No tracker or linker enters any detector claim. The ground point is image_to_pitch(u, v + size/2). In-flight balls read about 0.9 m further from the camera; this is documented, not corrected.

EVENTS INPUT: dense v2 rows with p_cal >= tau, top-k in {1, 4}, then one of two selections, the choice being part of the events grid:
1. v1 path: select_single_ball, then merge_fragments.
2. src/ball_link.link(rows, cal, players, c_null, c_static): a skip-Viterbi in pitch metres over the candidates plus a null state.
   - Unary: -logit(p_cal) + logit(tau).
   - Measurement σ = 1.5 px / min(sx, sy), clipped to [0.05, 1.0] m.
   - Transition: effective speed after a 2(σa + σb) slack. It is free up to 35 m/s, costs 4·(v/35 - 1)² above that, and is forbidden above 60 m/s.
   - Skips over up to 5 detection frames cost c_null per skipped frame.
   - Static penalty c_static: a candidate that has stayed within 0.5 m for >= 2 s and is >= 3 m from every pipeline-detected player.
   - Players come only from the pipeline's own detections.
   - Output: at most one ball row per frame.

This fixes the verified defect: select_single_ball uses one px_per_m on a view spanning about 2-72 px/m. The rest of the path is unchanged: to_pitch_metres, then detect_events(ball_time_aware=True).
results.events_protocol:
EVENTS PROTOCOL v3, registered within protocol v3 before training. The settings themselves are frozen after the sweep and before any V event.

E0. ORDER
- The detector is frozen.
- The V detector results are recorded in the doc.
- Events are tuned on U-E only.
- events_v3.json and its sha256 go into SOCCERTRACK_V2.md.
- One run on V.
- Dense v2 candidates on V-old exist before the freeze (they are used for detector scoring), but no events are computed from them until the freeze.

E1. WINDOWS
- U-E:
  - st2_118578_1st_f030000 (cached pipeline in events_v1);
  - st2_118578_2nd_f015000 (pipeline run once in step 4 with the same settings).
  - 86 pass+carry labels, 1 shot label. The v2 ball is out-of-sample there, as on V.
- V-E: the 2 V-old windows (cached pipelines): 130 pass+carry labels, 3 shot labels as in the doc.
- Players and teams are identical across all configurations; only the ball rows are swapped (score_soccernet.swap_ball_rows / events_from_cached).

E2. GRID (sweep_events_v2.py, staged, about 30 configs)
- A, ball input: top-k {1, 4} × selection {select_single_ball, ball_link(c_null 1, c_static 2)}.
- A2, only if the linker is chosen: c_null {1, 3} × c_static {2, 6}.
- B, possession: POSSESSION_RADIUS_M {2, 3, 4, 8} × MIN_POSSESSION_HOLD_S {0.2, 0.4}.
- C, pass and carry: CARRY_MIN_TIME_S {0.8, 1.2} × MIN_PASS_DISTANCE_M {0.3, 3}.
- D, shots, chosen by rate (too few labels for F1): SHOT_MIN_KMH {10, 30, 50} × SHOT_MAX_DIST_FROM_GOAL_M {50, 30} × SHOT_MOUTH_MARGIN_M {None, 5}. The ray must cross the goal line within ±(3.66 + margin) m. Take the most permissive setting with at most 3 shots pooled over U-E.
- Then re-check A with B-D fixed.
- Receiver, tackle and out rules stay at v1.

E3. OBJECTIVE
- Pooled pass+carry F1 at 1 s minus pooled chance F1 (200 random-time draws per window).
- Constraint: pass+carry events per window in [0.6, 1.5] × labels.
- Among configs within 0.02 of the best: fewest parameters changed from v1, then fewest events.
- Report per window and leave-one-window-out (choose on one window, score the other).

E4. GATE G-E
- The frozen config's objective must be >= that of v1 rules with the same v2 ball, on each U-E window separately.
- Otherwise C3 := C2 (v1 rules), disclosed.
- If the detector failed G, the whole sweep uses the best-on-U detector, disclosed.

E5. V CONFIGURATIONS
- C0: COCO + v1 rules (cached, 0.35).
- C1: v1 heatmap + v1 rules (cached, 0.44).
- C2: v2 + v1 rules.
- C3: v2 + frozen rules.
- C0': COCO + frozen rules. This is the ball-versus-rules decomposition.

E6. CLAIMS (events family, alpha 0.025 two-sided, fixed sequence)
- H3, C3 better than C0: pooled pass+carry F1 at 1 s, paired 10 s block bootstrap with 4,000 draws (score_events_paired.py). Rejected when the 97.5% lower bound is > 0.
- H4, C3 better than C1: tested only if H3 is rejected.
- Descriptive:
  - C2 and C0';
  - F1 against chance per window, with p;
  - tolerances 0.5 and 2 s;
  - event counts against labels;
  - shots against labels;
  - ball within 3 m of the actor;
  - team and actor accuracy.
- MDE stated in advance: about 0.18 F1 with 130 labels; about 0.13 if the optional extension windows are added (decided on time only, before any V event).

E7. AFTER V
- No rule edits after V.
- Any later change is a new protocol, scored on fresh M2/M10 minutes or deferred to M7/M9 by explicit decision.
dropped_ideas: Ranking/softmax term with a learned null logit (labels design). Broad bag mass satisfies it, it is one of many simultaneous loss changes that could not be told apart, and no ablation fits the budget.
Pseudo-label shrinking of flight bags, variant B (labels design). An untested moving part on a single seed; it would also spend U selection budget.

Constant-velocity blob miner with its own S1 mined-label blind gate (motion design). It needs an extra 100-tile sitting, its labels are biased toward easy isolated balls, and it does not fit 8 h. It can be added later behind its gate.

The labels design's 'size-invariant' unnormalised LSE pool (log(N)/r bonus for broad activation). Replaced by an LSE normalised by the ball's footprint (r 8, k 4); v1's log-mean-exp is kept for the small action and dribble bags.

The labels design's automatic measure (2.5 m | 20 px) as the tuning and co-primary measure. It is the training bag's own geometry and has no timing guard. Replaced by FF-auto (4 m, |t-s| <= 0.3), chosen on T by a stated rule.
The motion design's corridor-3m measure. No timing guard, it was validated on pooled T and V-old, and 2 of 65 decoys counted as hits on recomputation.

The motion design's corridor geometry: a 3 m band, passer and receiver ignored (feet stay in the bag), a 2 m chip extension, 256 px crops that drop near-side bags. Replaced by the labels design's geometry with every body outside the bag as a hard negative, and 320 px strips.

JPEG q95 strips (motion design). Replaced by q98 single-file strips with matched augmentation (one JPEG q across crops, independent per-crop noise), because frame differences of 4 px balls are fragile.

A no-motion ablation as a standard second training run (both judges). It costs about 1.4 h. Replaced by a free motion-zeroed inference diagnostic on U; an RGB-only run is trained only as the single fallback if the motion model fails G.

Linked picks in the detector claim (motion design). That would mix tracker and detector effects. Every detector is scored by raw top-1; the metric-space linker is an events-side option frozen before V.
The Kalman tracklet stage of the motion design's linker, and its 4x3 tuning grid. Simplified to a skip-Viterbi in pitch metres with a static flag, with 2x2 parameters inside the events sweep.
Fold detectors A/B for leak-free events tuning (protocol design). They cost about 4.5 h and give a weaker ball than v2. Replaced by tuning on held-out M6 windows with v2's own balls.

M5 as the tuning match (labels and protocol designs). It has the lowest pass rate (4.2/min), uncached 2nd-half GSR, and no cached player pipeline (an extra 1-2 h). M6 is used instead, with its COCO-distractor caveat disclosed and an absolute FF-auto bar in G1.

8 V-new windows and about 200 passes, plus 4 V events windows (protocol design / judge 2). Compute. Kept: 6 V-new windows (about 146 passes, MDE about 0.10); V events on the 2 cached V-old windows; 2 more events windows as a pre-registered, time-only optional extension.

Exact McNemar p<0.05 on about 60 tuning passes as a gate (motion design G2), and up to 2 further tuning iterations or 4 U variants. Underpowered and invites overfitting to U. Replaced by rate-based blind conditions, at most 2 trained variants and 1 fallback.

Blind primary on V-old's 38 passes with an automatic co-primary and Holm (labels design). Replaced by FF-auto as primary over about 146 passes, validity checked on clean V-new blind tiles, and a declared blind McNemar fallback on about 88 passes.
Resting-ball down-weighting as a separate detect_ball_heatmap flag (labels design). Subsumed by the linker's static penalty in the events grid.
Dropping FREE KICK action bags (motion design). Kept: motion dropout lets the RGB path find a static ball, and restarts matter for events.
A tau condition based on top-1 precision >= 0.8 (labels design). tau stays label-free (at most 1 candidate per frame on U random frames); Platt only rescales.
Motion blur augmentation (labels design). It is inconsistent across the 4 time crops; scale jitter is kept.
A second seed on U (protocol design optional). Budget; one seed is disclosed.
T as a tuning set. Demoted to a seen-match diagnostic with ±60 s guard bands, first in the cut order.
Blind judging of v1 on V-new and a 425-tile programme. Judge fatigue; v1 against v2 on V-new is measured by FF-auto (H2), and the V-old v1 judgements are reused. Total about 335 tiles in 3 sittings.

blocking.issue:
COMPUTE: the motion-stem costs are underestimated, so the 8 h budget breaks, and the declared cuts would eat the primary. I benchmarked the existing build() plus a 9->64 7x7/2 conv on this machine, which was otherwise idle.
- Training step, batch 16: 256 px 0.82 s; 320 px 1.18-1.26 s; 320 px with the 9-channel motion stem 1.44-1.71 s. That is +22-36%, not +18%.
- Full-frame forward (1000x4000, 2 threads): 2.4-2.5 s without motion, 3.1-3.6 s with it. That is +25-28%, not +7%.
- From the logs: v1 trained at 0.716 s/step (2147 s for 3000 steps), and its dense run took about 3,700 s per 3-min window, in parallel pairs.
Consequences:
(a) v2 cannot keep v1's frozen-stem saving, because conv1_motion trains from step 1, so backprop goes through layer1 to the stem from the start. Augmenting 4 crops of 320 px is about 6x v1's per-sample augmentation work. Realistic: 1.6-1.8 s/step, so 4,000 steps take 107-120 min, not 100.
(b) The dense v2 runs in step 10 cost about 1.28 x 62 = 80 min per window pair, so 2 pairs plus the background pass take about 170 min, not 140. The plan's own '68 min per window' is already below 1.07 x v1's 75 min.
(c) Step 9 runs 3 detectors on about 250 frames in each of 6 windows at about 1 s per frame, plus 2 decodes per window: about 50-60 min, not 35.
(d) Step 4 runs the full player pipeline on st2_118578_2nd_f015000 (no output_ directory exists, so detection is from scratch: about 2,250 yolov8s full-width frames, 40-75 min). It shares 4 cores with two half-streams and the COCO ignore pass on about 5,200 crops: about 100 min, not 70.
The base comes to about 9.5-10 h, and about 12 h with the fallback. Cuts 1-3 save under 30 min. Cut 4 removes 2 of 6 V-new windows: the MDE rises from about 0.10 to about 0.12, and the M2/M10 same-sign condition gets weaker.

non_blocking.issue:
TRAIN/INFERENCE MISMATCH IN THE MOTION CHANNELS. Training strips come from the source stream (PyAV decode, then JPEG q98). Every U and V input is a window mp4 that src/soccertrack_v2.write_clip re-encoded with x264 crf18. I measured 11 patches of the local M5 window st2_118577_1st_f030000 (frames 30100-30524):
- source patch vs window frame at the same pixels: mean absolute difference 3.3-4.1 grey levels;
- the window's own consecutive frames: mean absolute difference 2.3-4.6, median 0 (x264 copies static blocks exactly).
The codec gap is as large as the real frame-to-frame motion, and its noise is structured differently (exact zeros against JPEG plus the augmentation's sigma 0-2 noise). If the motion branch keys on codec texture, U G fails. That spends the fallback (about 2 h) and is not a finding about motion.
non_blocking.fix: Zero-cost check in step 4: when M5 half 1 is streamed, build the strips with frames 30000-34499 a second time from the local window mp4. Compare the per-channel D and F statistics, and the sigma constants, between the two sources, and log the result. If the D-channel scale differs by more than 1.5x, add an augmentation before training starts: pass the [t-2, t, t+2] crops through in-memory libx264 crf18 at crop size with p 0.5 (a few ms per strip). Record it in the provenance.

non_blocking.issue:
THE MEASURE AND THE TRAINING LABELS SHARE A GEOMETRY, AND THE PLACEBO DOES NOT TEST FOR THAT. v2's flight bags (|t-t_hat| about 0.25, within 2.5 m perpendicular, at least 1 m from feet) sit inside FF-auto's acceptance region (within 4 m, |t-s| <= 0.3, at least 1 m from persons). v1 and COCO were never trained toward that region. A learned pass-corridor prior (grass between passer and receiver, cued by follow-through pose and runs) would therefore count as hits for v2 only.
- The kick-15/kick-30 placebo comes before those cues exist, so it cannot catch such a prior.
- The S2 differential-bias check (point estimate <= +0.05 on about 50 tiles, SE about 0.06) passes a true bias of +0.10 about 20% of the time.
The 'clearly better' claim is protected by its blind >= +0.10 condition; H1 alone is not.
non_blocking.fix:
Add three measures to protocol v3 before training:
(a) A post-reception placebo at reception+15 frames. The top-1 counts as a placebo hit if it lies within 4 m of the just-completed segment with t in [0.1, 0.7] and at least 1 m from persons. Report it in G2, held to the same 0.05 bar.
(b) On S2 and S3 frames where one detector's tile is judged B, count the other detector's FF-auto hits that are more than 12 px from that confirmed ball. Each is a confirmed false hit of FF-auto, free from existing judgements, and is reported per detector.
(c) State the validity condition as the one-sided 90% upper bound of the differential bias <= +0.10, or report a bias-corrected FF-auto difference alongside H1.

non_blocking.issue: V-OLD LEAKS INTO THE LABELS AND THE MEASURE, AND V-OLD IS 26% OF THE H1 PASSES. The near/far split of the label constants was pooled with V-old judgements, so judged ball positions on M2/M10 shaped v2's training bags. The FF-auto kappas on V-old were also seen during design.
non_blocking.fix: Recompute the near/far constants from the T judgements alone, or T+U; it is a one-line change before the labels are built. Also require the FF-auto difference to be positive on V-new alone, as an extra condition for 'clearly better', and report V-new alone next to the pooled H1.

non_blocking.issue: THE SEAL CAN LEAK BEFORE JUDGING. eval_ball_detector.main() prints the whole summary to stdout: the legacy free-flight hit, the action hit and the paired difference. detect and validate also write logs. The person who judges S2 and S3 is the person who runs these, so a printed legacy 1 m score, which correlates with FF-auto, would be seen before the sittings. Separately, the V-new windows are cut in step 8, before G is decided. If the fallback runs, the detector is frozen after V-new exists.
non_blocking.fix: --sealed must write only to a sealed file and print nothing but frame counts and timing, for every measure including the legacy one, in eval, detect and validate_ff_auto alike. Move the V-new cut to after the G decision, or state in the protocol that it may precede a fallback freeze and that nothing from V-new is read until unseal.

non_blocking.issue:
EVENTS IMPLEMENTATION TRAPS.
(a) run_pipeline calls track_reid.merge_fragments after select_single_ball, and merge_fragments relabels PLAYER track ids. If the linker path replaces both calls, player identities differ between select='v1' and select='link', so the selection effect is confounded with player identity.
(b) Ball rows must be swapped in both tracks.parquet and tracks_teams.parquet, as e5.py does.
(c) The new scorer must reproduce the cached C0 = 0.35 and C1 = 0.44 exactly.
(d) Overriding module globals works for POSSESSION_RADIUS_M, MIN_POSSESSION_HOLD_S, CARRY_MIN_TIME_S and MIN_PASS_DISTANCE_M (read at call time). It would not work for constants bound as default arguments (e.g. _smooth_series' VEL_SMOOTH_WINDOW), nor for src/constants.py, which defines different values under the same names.
non_blocking.fix: In the link path, keep merge_fragments on the player rows and replace only the ball selection. Assert, with a hash of the player and team rows, that they are identical across every configuration. Add the C0/C1 reproduction as a regression in score_events_paired.py. In detect_events(params=...), whitelist the overridable names and raise on any name not in the whitelist.

non_blocking.issue:
EVENTS DESIGN.
(a) The grid's dimensions came from seeing V-old's events: 182 shots, 282 events against 130 labels, overfiring rules. The values are tuned on U-E, but V-old is not virgin for rule design.
(b) G-E requires the frozen rules to beat v1 rules on EACH U-E window. st2_118578_1st_f030000 is 2 minutes with 7 qualifying passes and 29 actions, so that half of the gate is close to a coin flip, and C3 := C2 will often follow from noise.
(c) The H3 MDE of about 0.18 means only a very large gain can be shown.
